The City partners with key higher education institutions such as the Ateneo de Davao University, University of Southeastern Philippines (USEP), University of the Philippines Mindanao, and other colleges and schools in Davao City to advance climate action and resilience. These institutions contribute through research, technical expertise, and extension programs, particularly in renewable energy, sustainable urban planning, climate-smart agriculture, disaster risk reduction, and ecosystem restoration.

Collaborations have resulted in tree-growing and watershed protection programs, school-based zero-waste and recycling campaigns, and community outreach activities in vulnerable barangays. For example, UP Mindanao has supported climate-smart agriculture and food security research, Ateneo de Davao has integrated climate and sustainability studies in policy advocacy and governance work, while USEP has partnered with the City in capacity development for disaster preparedness and resilience-building.

Progress includes the integration of climate change modules in academic curricula, expanded student and faculty-led research for policy support, and youth-driven initiatives such as water conservation, food security projects, and awareness campaigns on climate-sensitive health issues. These partnerships strengthen the City's local climate action planning and ensure long-term community engagement.

The City Government of Davao, through the City Agriculturist's Office, collaborates with the agriculture sector to strengthen climate resilience and ensure food security. Collaboration focuses on:
• Capacity development - Training farmers on climate-smart agriculture such as organic farming, integrated pest management, crop rotation, and the use of climate-resilient crop varieties (e.g., drought- and flood-tolerant rice and corn).
• Knowledge and data sharing - Providing farmers with access to localized weather and climate advisories through PAGASA and DA in coordination with the city's disaster risk reduction office.
• Project implementation - Supporting initiatives like urban container gardening, community-based seed banking, and agroforestry programs in upland barangays to restore degraded land and improve watershed protection.
• Technical assistance and financing - Extending farm mechanization support (e.g., small tractors, dryers), access to government grants and insurance (e.g., PhilCrop Insurance Corp. coverage), and facilitating linkages with agri-cooperatives and markets.
• Policy and program integration - Incorporating climate adaptation and DRR strategies into barangay-level agriculture development plans and aligning them with the city's Local Climate Change Action Plan (LCCAP).

Progress achieved:
• Adoption of organic and diversified farming systems has expanded, with more barangays certified as organic farming zones.
• Establishment of farmer field schools for hands-on training on climate-smart practices.
• Increased market access through the Agri-Fishery and Livestock Terminal and “Kadiwa sa Davao” initiatives, supporting local farm-to-market linkages.
• Improved resilience of smallholder farmers to climate impacts, reducing crop loss during extreme weather events.
• Strengthened collaboration with farmer cooperatives in watershed rehabilitation projects in areas such as Marilog and Paquibato.

The City of Davao has collaborated with the Food & Beverage sector through joint initiatives on sustainable food systems, food waste reduction, and local sourcing. Partnerships with restaurants, food processors, and retailers have been established to promote the “Zero Food Waste” campaign, where surplus food is redirected to community feeding programs and vulnerable groups instead of disposal.

The City Agriculture Office has initiated to link local farmers and fisherfolk directly to F&B establishments, ensuring stable markets for local produce while reducing emissions from long-haul transport. Some beverage companies have partnered with the LGU on plastic waste recovery programs and water stewardship initiatives, such as improving wastewater treatment and reusing process water.

Progress to date includes the signing of Memorandum of Understanding with selected F&B companies, pilot projects on food waste segregation and composting in key establishments, and the integration of local farmers into supply contracts of hotels and restaurants. Initial monitoring has shown a reduction in food waste volumes in partner establishments and an increase in the adoption of sustainable sourcing practices, benefiting both the local economy and the environment.

The City Government of Davao collaborates with Davao Light and Power Company (DLPC) in advancing renewable energy adoption, energy efficiency, and climate-resilient power systems. This partnership includes joint initiatives on solar rooftop projects in selected government facilities, upgrading streetlights to energy-efficient LED systems, and promoting awareness campaigns on energy conservation.

Through knowledge and data sharing, DLPC provides technical information on power demand and supply trends, which supports the City's climate action planning and monitoring of emissions reduction. Capacity development programs have also been undertaken with academic institutions and DLPC to train local stakeholders on energy-efficient technologies.

Recent progress includes the implementation of solar energy demonstration projects, expansion of LED streetlighting across major city roads, and collaborative studies on integrating renewable energy into the local grid. These initiatives contribute to emissions reduction, improved resilience against energy supply disruptions, and enhanced access to affordable, sustainable energy for Davao City communities.

Davao City, in partnership with the Department of Transportation (DOTr), Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB), Davao Light and Power Company (DLPC), and transport cooperatives, is actively implementing the Davao Public Transport Modernization Project (DPTMP). The collaboration focuses on the modernization of jeepneys into low-emission and electric vehicles, supported by knowledge sharing, technical assistance, and financing schemes for transport cooperatives.

Progress has been made through the route rationalization plan, which reorganizes existing routes for efficiency, and the establishment of integrated terminals and depots to improve connectivity and commuter convenience. Pilot testing of electric buses and modern jeepneys has been conducted in selected routes, while capacity development programs for drivers and operators were rolled out to support their transition to modern units and ensure livelihood continuity.

The City has also collaborated with DLPC and private partners on charging infrastructure for electric vehicles, aligning with the city's long-term vision of sustainable mobility and emissions reduction. These efforts are integrated into the City's climate action and resilience strategies, ensuring that transport modernization also addresses air quality improvement, commuter safety, and inclusive access to mobility services.

column17: Davao City works with barangays, NGOs, private contractors, and residents' associations to strengthen solid waste management as part of its climate action strategy. Through the City Environment and Natural Resources Office (CENRO), collaboration focuses on the establishment of Material Recovery Facilities (MRFs), community-based waste segregation campaigns, and plastic reduction initiatives that directly support emissions reduction by diverting biodegradable and recyclable materials away from landfills. Partnerships with the private sector and industry groups include recycling and waste-to-energy feasibility studies, while NGOs and community groups are engaged in capacity development and awareness programs to promote inclusive and equitable waste practices. Informal waste pickers are being integrated into organized cooperatives, creating social equity benefits alongside climate outcomes. Progress includes expanded MRF operations in barangays, pilot composting hubs that reduce methane from organic waste, increased compliance with segregation-at-source, and ongoing assessments of waste-to-energy potential. These collaborative actions enhance resilience by reducing landfill dependence, improve public health by minimizing waste-related pollution, and contribute to Davao City's broader circular economy and climate mitigation goals.

Davao City collaborates with the construction sector, particularly through partnerships with private developers, contractors, and professional organizations (e.g., Philippine Institute of Civil Engineers, United Architects of the Philippines), to promote green building practices and climate-resilient infrastructure development. The City implements and enforces the Green Building Ordinance of Davao City, which requires new developments to adopt sustainable design measures such as energy-efficient lighting, natural ventilation, water reuse systems, and proper solid waste management.

The City also works with the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH), construction firms, and academe to integrate disaster-resilient standards into housing, commercial, and public infrastructure projects. Progress includes the increasing number of buildings applying for green certification, pilot projects in rainwater harvesting, and the promotion of eco-friendly materials to reduce emissions from construction activities.

Ongoing collaborations support capacity development for local engineers and builders on climate-resilient design and public-private partnerships for major infrastructure projects, such as flood control systems, resilient road networks, and sustainable housing projects. These efforts are aligned with the City's Local Climate Change Action Plan (LCCAP) and Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Plan (DRRMP), ensuring that infrastructure development addresses both mitigation (emissions reduction) and adaptation (resilience to climate hazards) goals.

The City Government of Davao, through the City Planning and Development Office (CPDO), the City Engineer's Office, and the City Housing Office, collaborates with real estate developers and industry associations to promote sustainable and climate-resilient urban development. This collaboration focuses on integrating green building standards, renewable energy solutions, disaster-resilient design, and proper waste and water management systems in new housing and commercial developments.

To date, progress has been made through the implementation of the Green Building Ordinance and the integration of environmental compliance requirements in subdivision and building permits. Real estate developers are required to incorporate rainwater harvesting systems, energy-efficient lighting, ventilation, and tree-planting initiatives in their projects. In partnership with utility providers, select developments have piloted the use of solar rooftop systems and low-carbon construction materials.

Moreover, the City is actively engaging developers in transit-oriented development (TOD) planning, ensuring that new estates are accessible to public transport and aligned with sustainable mobility initiatives. There are also ongoing discussions for public-private partnerships (PPPs) to expand affordable and climate-resilient housing for vulnerable groups.

These efforts demonstrate the City's commitment to balancing urban growth with environmental stewardship, ensuring that Davao's real estate development contributes to both economic progress and climate action goals.

The Bike-to-School Program aimed to promote active transport among students and school personnel by providing safe and accessible cycling and walking routes in school zones within communities. The pilot project was conducted from August 2024 to April 2025 in the school zone of Judge Feliciano Belmonte Sr. High School (JFBSHS) in Barangay Holy Spirit, Quezon City. 

Key accomplishments include:
- More than 130 students directly involved in assessments and workshops
- Mapping of additional 60 meters of delineated pedestrian paths near the school gates
- Street design transformation test near the JFBSHS AFP Road Gate resulted in an increased Star Rating from 3 stars to 4 stars

Through the story of Uno, the book introduces children to the impacts of climate change on their daily lives and encourages simple actions for the environment, with content designed to be inclusive of children with disabilities. The book was launched on Araw ng Pagbasa (National Reading Day) with a reading session at P. Bernardo Elementary School attended by 160 students, alongside simultaneous activities across 325 daycare centers.\n\nIt has since been featured in other city programs, including the Good Food Fiesta, where the book was read to 2,500 daycare children to reinforce messages of environmental responsibility.

column17: Supported by UK Government funding (2022-2025), the Urban Climate Action Programme - Climate Action Implementation (UCAP CAI) accelerates the delivery of Climate Action Plans in 15 Global South cities, including Quezon City, in line with the Paris Agreement's 1.5°C target. Launched on August 12, 2022, the program has provided experts in green building, energy efficiency, and renewable energy to assist the City in implementing its priority actions.\n\nWith this support, Quezon City has already determined solar energy penetration and potential market demand in buildings, and developed a Solar Deployment Strategy (2025-2050). The City also amended its Green Building Code, completed the draft Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR), and is finalizing the development of green building incentives. Ongoing work under UCAP includes the preparation of a Climate Finance Guide and training modules, as well as the development of Monitoring, Evaluation, and Reporting (MER) tools for strategic high-impact and inclusive climate actions.

column17: Executive Order No. 16, S-2021 or the Healthy Public Food Procurement Policy of Quezon City was signed and issued last July 23, 2021. The policy contains the nutrition standards to be followed by the City Government and sets the roles of each Department involved. The policy also creates a healthy food system wherein healthy food and ingredients may also be sourced from the City's Urban Farms. This is an output of the city's partnership with ImagineLaw under Resolve to Save Lives, an initiative of Vital Strategies which is supported by Bloomerg Philantrophies, Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation, and the Zuckerberg-Chan Foundation. \n\nSeries of refresher trainings have been conducted in collaboration with the City Health Department and Procurement Department. These sessions were provided to all City Council Offices, City Departments, Barangays and government-owned hospitals, particularly ahead of the annual budget season, to reinforce adherence to the policy. The City Health Department continues to be consulted by these departments and monitors compliance, including local government hospitals and residential care facilities such as Molave Youth Home and QCHMB (milk-letting).

column17: In May 2023, the UN Environment Programme (UNEP), through the League of Cities of the Philippines (LCP), launched a competitive call for proposals to promote sustainable urban transitions using nature-based solutions (NbS). From over 240 submissions, Quezon City was selected as one of only eight global pilot cities, recognized for its innovative project concept. The initiative, called Generation Restoration, is a three-year program (2023-2025) that focuses on developing a Biodiversity and Urban Ecosystem Restoration Plan with the active involvement of biodiversity experts, local communities, youth, and other stakeholders.\n\nThe project designates the Payatas Controlled Disposal Facility (PCDF) as its pilot location, with the goal of transforming the former landfill into an ecopark. Phases of the project include capacity-building, science communication, and a citizen science program, with activities ranging from biodiversity assessments and stakeholder workshops to the co-design of restoration strategies by students and community members.

Through the said partnership, it has already enabled the utilization of over 1 million liters of treated wastewater for the City's watering operations. It conserves potable water, reduces costs, and demonstrates sustainable water management practices that support urban greening and climate resilience.

column17: The Quezon City Government partnered with Greenpeace Philippines to implement the Refill Revolution program, transforming local sari-sari stores into eco-friendly refill hubs. The program makes common household products such as liquid detergents, fabric conditioners, and dishwashing liquids available in bulk, encouraging customers to bring reusable containers and reduce single-use plastic waste or sachets. This collaboration promotes sustainable consumption practices at the community level while supporting the City's broader zero-waste agenda. In March 2024, the Quezon City Government enacted the Calorie Labeling Ordinance, making it the first local government in the Philippines to require restaurants and food businesses to display the calorie content of their menu items. The policy, which applies to fast food chains, restaurants, hotels, and other food establishments, aims to promote informed consumer choices and encourage healthier eating habits among its citizens.

The ordinance was developed through extensive public consultations with food establishments and restaurant associations in Quezon City, ensuring that the policy was both practical for businesses and responsive to consumer health needs. It mandates that calorie counts (in kilocalories) be clearly displayed on menus and menu boards, positioned near the name or price of each food item. Customers may also request additional nutrient information, including carbohydrates, fats, sugars, and sodium.

Implementation follows a phased rollout: large food chains by December 2025, smaller businesses and hotels in 2026, and full compliance by all food establishments in 2027.

The works were aimed at stabilising the drain embankments to prevent soil erosion and collapse, as well as reducing flood risk in the Section 19 industrial area (particularly at the downstream point of Jalan 19/1 towards Sungai Penchala). column17: Under city to city collaboration study, IRDA work together with Toyama City in introducing decarbonisation technologies in green mobility and electrical vehicle (EV) ecosystems through the introduction of Battery as a Service (BAAS). The expected outcome of this study was to propose appropriate decarbonisation technologies (Dual Diesel Fuel - DDF Kit) and determine the feasibility of using biofuel from the source of palm oil mill effluent (POME) as an alternative fuel for powering transportation and other sectors. The challenges and readiness on the ground were identified in the study. For way forward, the study suggested exploring biogas usage in the industry sector with the partnership with Gas Malaysia Berhad, Nihon Kucho Hokuriku Co. Ltd and Shinnihon Consultant Co. Ltd. BaaS (Battery as a Service) model to reduce the cost burden of the project proponent regarding the introduction of stations and to ensure the quality of the battery. It is a unique way that allows customers to keep their vehicles charged up and running, without having to worry about recharging drained-out batteries or replacing them. The concept enables customers to lease out batteries as a separate component from the car, on a subscription-based model, and swap it for a fully charged one as and when it depletes power.The concept makes for a great first step, for both businesses and customers, toward sustainability. While battery-powered vehicles undoubtedly reduce fossil fuel consumption, the BaaS model further helps to offset carbon emissions, with solar-powered charge stations, shared mobility services, and more. As a result, the data-driven BaaS model adds potential for flexibility and scalability for businesses and fulfilling experiences for customers.

column17: Iskandar Malaysia Ecolife Challenge (IMELC) is a high impact project organized by Johor State Education Department (JPNJ), Iskandar Regional Development Authority (IRDA) and Universiti Teknologi Malaysia (UTM) since 2013. IMELC aims to create awareness of Low Carbon Society (LCS) among students, teachers, and their families in achieving the target of carbon reduction for Iskandar Malaysia (IM) by the year 2025 as outlined in the Low Carbon Society Blueprint for Iskandar Malaysia 2025 (LCSBPIM2025). IMELC is a student learning activity on LCS that is conducted as formal or informal education in a school setting. It can also be conducted as a supplementary learning activity or inter-school competition. IMELC is a part of programs under the Johor Sustainability Education Action Plan 2019-2025 to develop a culture of sustainable development among the students and to achieve UN Sustainable Development Goals. Since 2021, IMELC has been digitalised and run fully through website sponsored by United Nations Development Programme or UNDP Accelerator Labs and supported by Green Technology Application of the Development of Low Carbon Cities (GTALCC). IMELC is also one of the key activities under RCE Iskandar - Regional Center of Expertise (RCE) on Education and Sustainable Development supported by United Nations University. IMELC starts with only 23 schools in 2013 and 2023 is the eleventh (11) year of IMELC implementation and will benefit approximately 100,000 Year 6 students from 907 primary schools in Johor. 2025 the school involvement increase to 909 primary schools in the state of Johor.\n Facebook link for Iskandar Malaysia IMELC: https://www.facebook.com/sustainablerceiskandar?mibextid=ZbWKwL

Lung health: Given that long-term exposure to suspended particulate matter (PM2.5, dust) may cause respiratory diseases (such as obstructive pulmonary disease, asthma, etc.) and increase the risk of lung cancer, and according to the National Health Administration: 'Once you suffer from chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, you are more likely to have comorbidities such as cardiovascular disease, osteoporosis, diabetes, and lung cancer.' Because chronic obstructive pulmonary disease progresses slowly and symptoms are easily ignored, in order to protect the lung health of citizens, the Health Bureau has cooperated with Taichung Veterans General Hospital from 2019 to 2023, combining local health centers, village offices and community development associations to continuously promote lung function screening services for citizens over 40 years old as a front-end prevention of lung health. These rooftop gardens not only beautify the environment but also help enhance climate resilience. Through rooftop greening, buildings can reduce heat island effects, lower summer air conditioning energy consumption, and assist with rainwater retention and infiltration, thereby easing urban drainage pressure. column17: In September 2020, the City of Tampere in collaboration with Business Tampere establised a Regional Climate Partnership -program. Since then over 100 companies and communities have joined the partnership. These include businesses from start-ups to big national and multinational companies in various sectors but also organizations and communities such as Tampere Universities and the federation of Tampere ev. luth. parishes. The goal of the Tampere region's climate partnership model is to involve companies and communities in the region in pursuing a carbon-neutral Tampere in cooperation with the city. The Climate Partnership is, as the name implies, a partnership; it is intended to benefit both parties to the partnership agreement. Climate partners themselves define their own organisation's climate action and goals related to climate change mitigation and/or adaptation. Partners can focus on what they want, such as energy savings, energy efficiency, environmental friendliness in procurement, waste management or staff involvement.The partnership is free of charge. To join, companies fill in a form where they accept to collaborate towards the goal of a carbon-neutral Tampere by 2030. Then, climate partners identify key emissions from their own operations and plan the most effective measures to reduce emissions. Every year, climate partners choose at least one of the emission reduction measures they will implement during the year. These measures will be then published on the website ilmastokumppanuus.fi and reported on at the end of the year. Climate partners are committed to continuously developing their operations to be more responsible in accordance with the principles of sustainable development, and they are encouraged communicate their climate actions to their customers / employees / members and other key stakeholders and provide opportunities for responsible operations and lifestyles.In return, companies and organizations that become climate partners in the Tampere region gain visibility on the Climate Partnership website and through Business Tampere. In addition, climate partners receive the latest information on climate issues and come up with a nationally and internationally significant theme, with opportunities to present their own activities and network at various events organized for them throughout the year. Climate partnership is also a competitive advantage that attracts new customers to explore the services offered by companies.

The Uppsala Climate Protocol is a local network uniting public and private sectors, civil society organizations, and academia to reduce emissions and limit global warming to 1.5 degrees. Launched in 2010 and comparable to a local Paris Agreement, its membership has grown from 17 to 49, representing all major workplaces in the city.
The protocol targets key areas: energy, transport, construction, and workplace operations, defining Climate Challenges for members to adopt based on relevance. Its focus and working groups facilitate collaboration, inspiration, and knowledge exchange. Emphasizing innovation and knowledge sharing, the UCP conducts regular workshops, seminars, and collaborative projects to foster idea exchange, technological development, and implementation of advanced climate solutions.
The focus group for climate neutral building and development has developed and taken on challenges including building more with timber frame, reducing emissions from steel and cement, and reducing emissions from building plastics. They are also collaborating on a common reporting standard for emissions per building project, which has improved benchmarking and the ability for parties to demand that building projects do not exceed a certain limit of CO2e/m2.

The UCP has set a yearly emission reduction target of 14%, now adjusted to 20% due to unmet goals. From 2017 to 2020, the total reduction was 26%. Between 2021 and 2024, emissions were reduced by 22% in scopes 1 and 2, and 8% overall including scope 3, primarily from decreased emissions in transport and energy use.
Through these efforts, Uppsala aims to significantly reduce carbon emissions, setting a strategic direction and fostering a community-wide commitment to a low-carbon future.

The Open Academy (Öppen Akademi) initiative is part of the broader Climate-Neutral Cities 2030 programme. It is designed to strengthen collaboration between municipal administrations, universities and other knowledge actors. In Helsingborg, this work is carried out in close partnership with Lund University, Malmö and Lund municipalities. 

The purpose of the initiative is to create an open arena where academics and practitioners co-produce knowledge, explore transformative practices and develop education and research agendas that directly support the climate transition. The Open Academy organises thematic dialogues, joint research projects and experimental activities that connect municipal needs with scientific expertise. 

By engaging researchers and students in real urban challenges, Helsingborg ensures that its climate actions are evidence-based and informed by the latest academic insights. At the same time, the initiative provides universities with opportunities to test new educational formats, cross-disciplinary collaboration and innovation methods in practice.

Helsingborg Climate Agreement (Helsingborgs Klimatavtal) 
The Helsingborg Climate Agreement is a local partnership model that engages businesses, organisations and associations in the city's climate transition. Signatory organisations commit to reducing their greenhouse gas emissions in line with Helsingborg's goal of climate neutrality by 2030. 

As of today, more than one hundred companies and associations have joined the agreement. The process is voluntary but based on mutual responsibility: organisations pledge concrete actions, while the City of Helsingborg provides facilitation, coordination and platforms for knowledge exchange. Regular network meetings, thematic workshops and joint communication initiatives support partners in identifying solutions and accelerating the shift to sustainable business models. 

The agreement strengthens cross-sectoral collaboration by creating a shared framework for monitoring progress and celebrating achievements. It has become an important driver of innovation and competitiveness in the local business community, while ensuring that the climate transition is inclusive and co-owned by a wide range of stakeholders.

The Helsingborg Declaration is a strategic collaboration platform through which businesses commit to supporting Helsingborg's broader sustainability goals. It was launched during the H22 City Expo in 2022 as a way to mobilise the private sector in addressing the city's long-term challenges. 

By signing the declaration, companies confirm their willingness to contribute to Helsingborg's development in areas such as climate, social inclusion, innovation and resilience. Viable Cities 
Helsingborg is a partner city in Viable Cities - Climate-Neutral Cities 2030, Sweden's largest national research and innovation programme for climate-neutral and sustainable cities. The programme is jointly financed by the Swedish Energy Agency, Vinnova and Formas, and involves almost 50 Swedish municipalities working together towards climate neutrality by 2030. 

Through this partnership, Helsingborg participates in knowledge exchange, shared learning and experimentation with other municipalities and academic institutions. The city collaborates closely with Malmö, Lund and Lund University in the establishment of a regional “Learning Hub,” which strengthens research-based policy development and the integration of science into municipal strategies. This co-production of knowledge allows Helsingborg to test innovative governance models, new financial solutions, and citizen-oriented approaches in real-world conditions. 

Participation in Viable Cities provides Helsingborg with a national platform to benchmark progress, engage in peer-to-peer learning and strengthen its capacity to accelerate the climate transition. The programme also connects local actors - including businesses, civil society organisations and universities - to national and international innovation ecosystems, thereby ensuring that Helsingborg's climate actions are embedded in both local priorities and broader systemic change.

Sunderland City Council has set up the 2030 Shadow Board with representatives from key organisations across the city, including the local NHS Foundation Trust, the University of Sunderland, Sunderland College (Education Partnership NE), North East England Chamber of Commerce (an independent business membership organisation representing over 3,000 businesses in North East England), Voluntary Sector Alliance, Together for Children, Transport NE, Sunderland Youth Council as well as cross-party Elected Member representation from each Group on the City Council and representation from the EGS group (more information available at https://www.mysunderland.co.uk/article/20627/Environmental-Green-and-Sustainable-Group). The 2030 Shadow Board's purpose is to work collectively to drive forward Sunderland's ambitions and commitment to tackling climate change.

Each partner is continuing to implement its own action plan and is actively carrying out low-carbon and climate adaptation initiatives to help enable the city to reach its low carbon and climate resilience goals. Current partner action plans can be found at Working together - MySunderland. The partnership meets on a quarterly basis and ensures that best practice is shared, and joint working is maximised.
In 2025, Sunderland City Council continued to coordinate and facilitate a range of partner deep dive sessions with other key organisations represented on the Shadow Board. These are identifying areas for deeper collaboration (data sharing, adaptation, communications, tree planting etc.) and have included work with the University of Sunderland; Gentoo housing provider; NHS Foundation Trust, Police and Fire Service and voluntary and health partners. The Council continues to convene a communications officer group which brings together leads from all Shadow Board members to work on citywide messaging and key sustainability campaigns.
It was the Shadow Board which requested and supported the foundation of the EGS group, referred to earlier. Whilst significant input is provided by Together for Children, the College and University, all partners on the 2030 Shadow Board committed to support its work and identify opportunities to engage young people through their own activity. 
Shadow Board partners continue to collaborate to support citywide initiatives including EcoFest and We Love Cities.

Building on the Council's successful delivery of the Business Renewables Energy Efficiency Sunderland (BREEZ 1) and the regional Business Energy Saving Team (BEST) programmes (2019-2023) Sunderland City Council continued to support local business and community organisations with UKSPF-funded BREEZ 2 from January 2024 to March 2025. 

BREEZ 2 supported the local business and community sectors with 50% (and in some instances up to 100%) grants to install a broad range of cost-effective, low carbon energy efficiency measures all of which were delivered via direct consultation with the Council. The primary objective of BREEZ is to upgrade old, inefficient heating, lighting and insulation systems with new, energy-efficient upgrades. BREEZ also provides 50% grant funding towards microgeneration (e.g., Photovoltaics) and upgrades for business process equipment. BREEZ also ensures the applicant, and their selected local contractor take responsibility for calculating and realising the cost-effectiveness, energy savings and carbon reduction of proposed measures by including calculation templates in the BREEZ application pack. 

From January 2024 to March 2025 Sunderland City Council BREEZ 2 supported 84 local businesses and 35 community organisations (Total 119) with energy audits, advice and guidance. £513,191 of grant funding was allocated which attracted £609,130 match funding from grant beneficiaries. A grand total of £1.12m was invested in cost effective energy efficiency measures reducing carbon emissions by 333 tonnes a year whilst also significantly and sustainably cutting the energy bills of beneficiary organisations over the lifetime of the energy efficiency measures installed. 
 
BREEZ 2 involved ongoing collaboration between project staff from the Council and the wider Business Investment Team, External Funding & Compliance colleagues and Community networks. 

The successful delivery of BREEZ 2 in 2024/25 has enabled the council in 2025/26 to secure an additional £241,000 of UKSPF grant funding to deliver BREEZ 3 and support even more local businesses and community organisations. From April 2025 to date the BREEZ 3 project continues to deliver outcomes and is currently actively engaged with a further 56 new applicants with over £50,000 of grants already offered for investment in energy efficiency measures. The programmes is on target to complete in March 2026 at which stage we can report all outputs including total carbon savings.

More information on BREEZ 3 can be found at https://www.sunderland.gov.uk/Breez

The North East Transport Plan (NETP) was adopted by the elected mayor and Cabinet in March 2025. The Plan sets out priorities and forms the basis for bids and requests for funding for transport investment in the North East up to 2040.

The plan is structured around five key areas:
•	journey planning and customer support
•	ticketing and fares
•	expanding infrastructure and making it more resilient
•	enhancing safety, especially for women and girls
•	improving links between different modes of transport
The Transport Plan is supported by a number of focused strategy documents:

Making the Right Travel Choice The Making the Right Travel Choice Strategy encourages car users to switch one journey a week to a more sustainable travel option.

Bus Service Improvement Plan The North East Bus Service Improvement Plan (BSIP) outlines the region's ambitions and investment plan to make buses a more attractive alternative to private vehicles. The numerous measures proposed include improvements to timetables and fares, extensive priority measures on roads and at junctions to speed buses up - including two new Park & Ride sites, a set of affordable fare “caps” that work across all buses and Metro services, lower fares for many young people and simplified and improved information.

Sunderland City Council is working with Nexus and bus operators to improve bus service infrastructure and bus services by introducing low/zero carbon bus vehicles, real time information and integrated ticketing. Sunderland City Council is also working with neighbouring local authorities to enable cross boundary ticketing and Wi-Fi improvements, making the bus a more attractive choice. In a joint project between SCC, Nexus and NECA, a new bus route was created in July 2024, funded by the Government as part of the Bus Service Improvement Plan. This service strengthens links with Sunderland Royal Hospital, the International Advanced Manufacturing Park (IAMP), the Nissan car plant, Sunderland city centre, and Jarrow and Hebburn town centres.
Consultation on two corridor-based interventions in Sunderland is now complete. These interventions provide improved bus priority measures on the A690 (Durham Road) and A183 Chester Road with a total investment of approximately £3.1m Further detail regarding specific sustainable transport schemes currently being delivered in Sunderland can be found throughout the BSIP.

Zero Emission Vehicle Strategy The Northeast Zero Emission Vehicle (ZEV) Strategy aims to deliver reliable public ZEV charging infrastructure across the North East wherever people need it.

Active Travel Strategy The North East Active Travel Strategy aims for walking, wheeling and cycling to become the natural first choice for short everyday trips.

Rail and Metro Strategy The North East Rail and Metro Strategy sets out how rail and Metro can play a key role in achieving our region's shared transport vision and objectives. Funding has been approved at regional level to progress an Outline Business Case for the Washington Metro Loop by March 2027, and to produce a Strategic Outline Business Case for the Southern part of the Leamside Line. 

A Local Cycle and Walking Infrastructure Plan has been developed by Sunderland City Council, and this document sets out a strategy and delivery plan to improve Cycling and Walking networks in the city. 16km of new high-quality cycle routes are programmed for construction by March 2027, with a total investment of £23.2m. 

In 2024 the North East successfully secured £19.5m of investment through the Levelling Up Fund for a Transport Decarbonisation package. This multi-million pound investment will greatly enhance zero carbon options for local people, delivering up to 52 new high-quality electric buses which will travel on some of the region's most heavily congested routes, alongside 92 new Electric Vehicle (EV) chargers - many at key destinations such as Park and Ride sites - to encourage multimodal journeys. It is hoped expanded EV charging infrastructure will encourage more people to consider switching to a zero-emission vehicle where possible. 20 new electric buses are now in service in Sunderland serving routes between Sunderland and South Tyneside.

Sunderland is actively seeking to facilitate investment in industrial innovation and production linked to the electrification of advanced manufacturing, reflecting the City's leading role in EV production and battery manufacturing. The primary focus for this investment is centred around the Nissan and AESC plants, the International Advanced Manufacturing Park and Hillthorn Business Park.
The International Advanced Manufacturing Park (IAMP) is now part of the NE Investment Zone which was announced by UK Government in Nov 2023 focused on clean energy (offshore & renewable technologies) and green manufacturing (EV & battery production), forming part of the wider International Advanced Manufacturing Strategic Site (IAMSS). IAMP creates significant scope for large-scale production and assembly of new environmental technologies that are being developed in the area, with JATCO having announced establishment of JATCO UK at IAMP in Jan 2025 representing investment of £48.7m and creation of 183 skilled jobs once fully operational to supply electrified powertrain to Nissan - in premises built speculatively by SCC to attract such investment. The IAMP is being brought forward by SCC and South Tyneside Council, with developer HBD. 
SCC has also co-developed MADE NE, a £14.6m collaborative skills and industrial innovation project focused on EV and battery manufacturing, which was approved in July 2024 as part of the NE Investment Zone with initial activity now underway. Sunderland played a key co-design role in bringing the partnership together, securing regional Investment Zone support and funding, earmarking premises and contributing to initial business development and curriculum planning. MADE NE is designed to become self-sustaining after 5 years and its Advisory Board is currently chaired by SCC. It will bring together industry, colleges and universities from across the region to create a step change in skills development for electrification and advanced manufacturing.
The JATCO UK and MADE NE announcements follow earlier announcements by both Nissan and AESC. In July 2021 AESC announced that they would be building their 2nd gigaplant on IAMP with 9GWh of production capability which will create 700 jobs and safeguard a further 300 jobs. This was part of a wider announcement by Nissan regarding the creation of Nissan 36Zero in Sunderland. This inward investment announcement, which alongside JATCO UK investment will increase the city and region's green economy and support decarbonisation of transport, followed significant co-operation SCC and both Nissan and AESC as well as central government. Construction work is almost complete on site at IAMP on the new gigaplant. AESC followed this up in 2024 with a planning application as part of their feasibility study for an additional gigafactory on land adjacent to the plant under construction. In Nov 2023 Nissan announced its intention to produce 3 new models at its Sunderland plant as the company continues to transition to full electrification.
Sunderland is home to a range of fast-growing, innovative SMEs working at the leading-edge of the electrification of the automotive and other sectors. Advanced Electric Machines (AEM) is a spin-out from Newcastle University that manufactures electric motors and drive technologies in the city. AEM employs more than 50 people in a facility with space to annually produce 12,000 next generation electric motors - and played a key role in the initial development of the Driving the Electric Revolution (DER) programme and NE Industrial Centre working with Newcastle University, the NE Automotive Alliance and SCC. The 'Driving the Electric Revolution' national programme is specifically intended to facilitate projects in the field of Power Electronics, Machines & Drives and enable the UK to capture part of the significant global market opportunity which electrification represents.
In 2021, Turntide acquired Sunderland based Hyperdrive Innovation. Nurtured in the city until all operations were consolidated into their Gateshead owned facility in 2025, the company designs and produces lithium-ion battery packs and battery management systems and recently won a contract to supply Hitachi Trains to power the 1st battery powered trains in the UK. 
The Port has established itself as a hub for circular economy activity, with a growing cluster of businesses linked to SAF, and material recycling. The 'Trinity Rail, Road & Sea Enterprise Zone'—a brownfield development site within the Port—is ready for occupation and capable of supporting up to 20,000 sq.m. of low-carbon industrial floorspace, offering an Intermodal transport connectivity to reduce logistics-related emissions. Construction is progressing on a £100 million end-of-life tyre recovery facility by Norwegian company Wastefront. The facility will convert waste tyres into recovered carbon black and tyre derived oil, while creating 30+ local jobs.

This is designed to maximise the learning available to the city to support effective implementation and delivery in key priority areas.

Sunderland was invited to participate in the 2024 'We Love Cities' campaign and was delighted to be named Global Winner of the One Planet City Challenge, alongside Istanbul, Turkey. Over 900 cities from 70 countries took part in the challenge.

'We Love Cities' is a public engagement campaign that allows people across the world to express support for sustainable urban development by voting for their favourite finalist from WWFs One Planet City Challenge and posting improvement suggestions for these cities. 
The central aim of the campaign is to: 
• inspire and raise awareness for the sustainability progress being made in cities; 
• give the general public an opportunity to celebrate, vote and upgrade their city through making suggestions to decision makers; 
• reward communities and strengthen the bond between the public and decision makers. 
 
Sunderland developed a communications plan to ensure the campaign was widely shared in a range of formats and promoted other activities to sit alongside it (such as school posted competitions with finalists displayed around the city). Sunderland also worked with a diverse range of partners to ensure maximum engagement in the campaign, including the Environmental, Green and Sustainable (EGS) group. The campaign was also presented at the 2030 Shadow Board with partners from all sectors committed to its rollout.
The city was also named as the UK's National Winner of WWF's One Planet City Challenge (OPCC) 2024. 

The OPCC is one of the largest and longest-running climate challenges for local governments in the world. Since its inception in 2011, it has been highlighting leading examples of climate mitigation and adaptation from cities around the world. 

Over 350 local governments from nearly 50 countries participated in the competition, with the jury ranking cities based upon: 
•	Alignment of cities' targets with the Paris Agreement 
•	Inclusion of a well-balanced climate action plan to support achieving stated goals 
•	Coherence in climate action strategies 
•	Mainstreaming of climate action in the city administration, as well as reinforcement through stakeholder dialogue 
•	Leadership in terms of being open and innovative, and aiming to influence climate action beyond the city's own borders. 
The WWF jury found Sunderland's approach to climate action to be ambitious, multi-dimensional and well-balanced, scoring positively across all sectors.

Sunderland continues to ensure that a range of free climate-related opportunities are made available to all Sunderland schools. SCC circulate information on relevant sustainability-related climate opportunities, funding and initiatives at local, regional, national and international level. 
 
For example, the Waste and Recycling Visitor Education Centre have delivered 32 waste themed sessions with Sunderland schools in the 24/25 school year. Students have taken part in part in site visits, waste crafts, litter picks, waste assemblies, waste workshops, composting and food growing workshops. 
 
Other carbon-cutting opportunities shared in 2024/25, include the National Education Nature Park, Let's Go Zero, Climate Ambassadors, The Ministry of Eco Education, Count Your Carbon, Climate Friendly Schools, Leadership for Sustainability Training, the Woodland Trust's Free Trees programme, Eco Schools, Keep Britian Tidy initiatives, Parkthatbike, Walk to School Week, school competitions (e.g. WWF's We Love Cities, Big Battery Hunt) and tree planting opportunities. 
 
Launched during COP27 (November 2022), SCC commissioned and funded the Sunderland Climate Friendly Schools (CFS) programme, giving in-depth support to 10 primary/secondary/special schools in the city to form climate teams, undertake audits complete a whole school assembly, undergo staff training and form action plans to reach CFS status. 
Initially led by Outdoor and Sustainability Education Specialists (OASES), the programme supports children and young people to have the knowledge, confidence and skills required to drive the city's low carbon ambitions forward. 
Kepier, St Anthony's Girls Catholic Academy, Portland Academy, Albany Village Primary School, Barmston Village Primary School, Barnes Junior School, Hetton Lyons Primary School, Hudson Road Primary School, Seaburn Dene Primary School and Wessington Primary School took part in the CFS project and received intensive support to develop their curriculum and make climate-friendly changes from 2022-2024. 
 
School actions are based around 7 climate themes including energy, transport, building, water, food, consumption, and grounds. Climate actions schools have delivered include developing schools gardens, introducing plants into the classroom, teaching children about future green careers, promoting uniform/ costume swap shops, installing a water butt to harvest rainwater, energy saving school switch off, investigating renewable technologies, food waste programmes, and planting trees. 
 
All 10 CFS Schools have attained CFS status for 2 years of activities, working towards year 3. 
 
Alongside CFS, 5 other Sunderland schools (St Aidan's Catholic Academy, Harry Watts Academy, Ryhope Junior School and St Benet's RC Primary School) supported the development of a Wear Sustainable resources toolkit, including lesson plans for all key stages, loans box and trails. These are free and accessible to Sunderland schools. 
 
Following successful engagement with the first 10 Sunderland CFS, SCC committed to embedding the programme by funding a new cohort of 5 schools to take part in CFS from September 2024, whilst supporting the first cohort to achieve the year 3 award. This has included drawing down school support from Sunderland's Low Carbon Lead Teachers (Associate School Improvement Advisors), supporting their professional development. 
 
Diamond Hall Infant Academy, Benedict Biscop CE Academy, Southmoor Academy and North View Academy have taken part in the project this year. 
 
Alongside this, SCC has continued to run and grow the Sunderland Climate Friendly Schools Network through a mixture of online and in person sessions, cascading free resources and opportunities to all schools, as well as providing a space for schools to share best practice. 
 
This year, SCC has worked with Together for Children to embed climate change education and action within the Sunderland Healthy Schools Award, which has seen the development and launch of the Sunderland Low Carbon Charter Mark. This Charter is one of six Charter Marks within the Sunderland Healthy Schools Award. The Charter Mark is a tool for implementing sustainable practices into school life, from curriculum changes to community outreach and giving young people the tools they need to build a greener future. Several schools have already expressed an interest in getting involved. 
 
The Charter was officially launched in June 2025, at the Sunderland School Climate Conference, featuring 'Sunny Bee', a climate-conscious mascot inspired by children's artwork submitted at last year's conference and chosen by the Environmental, Green and Sustainable Group. 
 
22 Sunderland schools attended the second annual conference, where pupils took part in climate-themed activities, best practice sharing and networking with climate education organisations. 105 Pupils and 35 members of Teaching Staff attended the conference, along with 12 Organisations

Since its launch in 2021, the My Sunderland website continues to develop and is the citywide platform to allow partners to publish their data and detailed delivery plans in one place. (https://www.mysunderland.co.uk/LowCarbon). The website is interactive and provides regular reporting (including quarterly emissions reports, annual data reports, the city's annual CDP submission and the biannual One Planet City Challenge Strategic Feedback Report), case studies, partners involved, information on how to help and how we can help, information regarding the science of climate change and an events calendar to support awareness raising and engagement activity. The website is regularly updated to provide the latest information, science and events, as well as information regarding how residents can get involved in Low Carbon and sustainable living activity within the city. It also includes a section regarding how residents can get involved in sustainability.
The Council also distributes a fortnightly newsletter to all residents via email, and each communication includes a Low Carbon Sunderland section, encouraging residents and communities to support as well as promote projects and investments, which are progressing in the city and supporting residents to live sustainably. 

In January 2025, Sunderland Council launched its Green Business Toolkit. Businesses have free access to a self-service toolkit which is located online: Low Carbon: Green Business Toolkit - MySunderland. The Green Business Toolkit provides businesses with advice on measures to become more sustainable and reduce its impact on the environment, funding opportunities, signposts to external support, training and accreditation opportunities and case studies of Sunderland businesses. As of July 2025, the toolkit has had over 650 views.

Sunderland businesses can join the Sunderland Green Network for free, to obtain tailored support from the Council's Low Carbon team to calculate their carbon footprint and create a carbon reduction report from the data obtained. The network is also a place for businesses to connect and share best practice in sustainability with quarterly network meetings. As of August 2025, 15 businesses have signed up to the network, and through engagement with our Business Investment Team we will continue to increase awareness of the toolkit and network.

column17: The Council continues to work closely with Better Points, an app that tracks travel movements via GPS using smartphones and rewards participants with points for using more sustainable modes of transport like walking, cycling and using public transport as a pilot project. Extended until December 2025, currently (July 2025) there are 4,011 registered users and engagement rates have been very high throughout the project. In 23/24 a total of 307,392 sustainable trips were recorded covering 488,195 miles. After 10,785 trips we asked 'did this replace a solo car journey?' and 6,407 responses (59%) were 'yes'. Extrapolated, this suggests 290,000 car trips and 61.6 tonnes of CO2 emissions were avoided. The value of the latter, according to DESNZ, is £15,770 and the top 3 modes are walking (75%), cycling (9%) and bus (12%). Sunderland University and Sunderland College have partnered with BetterPoints and offer free drinks in their campus cafes when redeeming points, with competitions and bonus prizes to encourage students to travel actively. Active Sunderland and other big events taking place across the City are promoted with push notifications whereby users are rewarded with extra points for travelling to them sustainably for example The Big Walk, The Big Bike Ride and on match days to the Stadium of Light.

In March 2023 Sunderland City Council launched a new Green Champions program for employees. 
Early activities included recruitment of interested volunteers at three staff events, where the Council's and city's Low Carbon ambitions, framework and plans have been shared as well as information on specific Low Carbon topics (Active and sustainable transport in May and July 2023 and Reducing Consumption and Waste with links to Refill Sunderland and Plastic free month in July). 
Other staff have been recruited through participation in the Sunderland 60 Common Purpose Legacy projects (2023, 2024 & 2025), where young Council employees were invited to become Green Champions for their work areas. 
The Council's Green Champions network continues to grow. Meetings have included new participants from City Planning, Social Services, Human Resources and Organisational Development, and Regulatory Services among others taking the total number Green Champions to 42 (August 2025). 
Green Champions have been consulted on areas where their input is valuable, including the staff induction process for all new starters in which a face-to-face interactive session on Low Carbon and sustainable regeneration is now included monthly. They continue to feedback and support the iLearn online training module which is now available for all Council staff and includes information on both climate science and actions in the workplace/locally. 
The Green Champions are also continuing to identify areas where sustainable improvements can be made within their own diverse service areas - these have included postal system reviews, allotment provision and support, uniform swaps, and equipment recycling. Green Champions are also participating in the creation of media content to ensure staff comply with recycling in City Hall and other council workplaces (July 2025). 
 
Meetings are held on a quarterly basis (Jan, Apr, July, Oct), and key speakers are invited to discuss an area of interest. Topics discussed this year have included the Links With Nature Project, the role of the Voluntary Community Sector, Active Travel & Transport, and Coast projects. 
A Network has been created to run concurrently, for tenants of the City Hall Building, led by Knight Frank. The City Hall Green Champions Tenants meetings are a vehicle to share best practice and lead on all things sustainable.

In 2024, Sunderland's City Hall was awarded a prestigious environmental award for its efforts to reduce emissions and embrace sustainable practices. Construction at Riverside Sunderland was awarded the Silver Accreditation by the Investors in the Environment Scheme (iiE), as through to completion, ecological responsibility measures have been proactively put in place to improve the building's environmental impact from the offset.

Information relating to the city's low carbon journey continues to be available for staff to access via a Council digital hub and it is embedded into the Council's induction programme, alongside the roll out of Carbon Literacy Training for senior managers across the Council.

Sunderland City Council signed the UK100 pledge in February 2022, renewing its earlier pledge. This commits us to becoming net zero as a Council by 2030, as well as achieving net zero as a city by 2045. 

UK100 supported a range of initiatives for climate action, including the 'Local Climate Engagement' (LCE) programme, which is a partnership with Involve, the Democratic Society, Shared Future and Climate Outreach and was working with local authorities to deliver high-quality public engagement projects on climate policy in a way that benefitted both them and their local communities.
Following a successful bid in January 2022, Sunderland was one of 21 local authorities selected across the two LCE programmes from 75 applications and one of only 5 authorities to be offered the opportunity for in-depth project support for which it applied. 
Sunderland's project focused on public engagement around sustainable travel behaviours. The project has provided training to approximately 20 Council and Together for Children colleagues, some virtually and some in person from a range of services areas. Participants formed 3 focused teams to plan engagement on three separate projects including social prescribing for active travel (which is partly funded by the Healthy Cities Grant), cycleway design at Dame Dorothy Street to support the Local Cycling and Walking Infrastructure Plan (LCWIP) and home to school transport for SEND children and young people.

Social Prescribing: The project (Wear Moving) is working in Redhill and Southwick and activities continue to be delivered until the end of Summer 2025. The project provides social prescribing for active travel, supporting residents in North Sunderland to increase their participation in active travel - walking and cycling. SARA - Southwick and Community Opportunities Ltd are also delivering additional walking and cycling activities that will complement the already existing activities being provided by Sunderland Young Peoples Bike Project in Thompson Park and Sunderland Community Action Group based at St Peters Bike Dock. The Wear Moving pilot has successfully engaged a significant number of people in the North area of Sunderland, encouraging more walking and cycling in these targeted wards. 
Cycleway Design: 
Ryhope Road Public Consultation event took place on 26th February 25 with members of the design team, future Infrastructure team, active travel team, gateway wheelers disability group and Sustrans. The session was held at Back on the Map in Hendon where a high turnover of residents from the local area attended. 
Home to School Transport for SEND Children: Over the last couple of years, the demand for free transport has grown exponentially whilst the cost of providing taxis/minibuses has also increased. Taxis and minibuses may provide short term solutions for young people but sometimes doesn't enable them to develop essential independent skills that they will need as they leave formal education. A Project Officer in SEND Transport has been recruited to work on the Independent Travel Training project. The project is currently looking at the funding and further recruitment to help the scheme cover a wider scope of young people within the area. Capital funding being utilised to purchase 2 minibuses. 
ParkThatBike project collaboration between Public Health and Active Travel Team has been hugely popular in Sunderland to encourage residents to be more active and cycle more. Local organisations, community groups, health buildings, schools and education buildings apply for FREE cycle parking. This includes cycle racks, planters and secure storage sheds. As of August 2025, 108 organisations have applied with 169 cycle parking units supplied across the City. 
Active Sunderland deliver the bikeability programme to primary schools across the City and our Road Safety Team arrange balance bike training, engage with schools on a number of initiatives to encourage them to complete their school travel plan.

The Eco Fest programme grows from strength to strength each year. The festival which focuses on family centred activity has grown to include an Eco Shopping Mall in 2025. The event spans two sites, Sunderland Museum & Winter Gardens, and The Pavilion in Keel Square and has grown from 14 exhibitors to 32. 
The museum site hosts family activities in “zones” such as transport, energy and local growing activities, and the Pavilion hosts the Eco Shopping experience which includes traders with an eco-message. 
The zones and family activities aim to support our residents to make more sustainable life choices, by raising awareness of how small everyday changes can make a difference. 
The Eco Shopping Experience helps to support residents change their shopping habits and buy sustainable, environmentally friendly products. 
 
The Eco Fest builds on activity in previous years activities, which in 2023 saw 6 secondary schools and 2 primary schools design and deliver a range of carbon-cutting initiatives, from planting trees to creating orchards, reducing single-use plastics, and harvesting willow. 
Ecofest 2024 involved families and children in a recycling competition, with the most creative winner having their design displayed at the museum. 
Sunderland City Council is also demonstrating leadership of carbon accounting and reduction, through collaboration with Sunderland University, a member of the 2030 Shadow Board. The Council is connecting businesses within the voluntary and community sector with the university, allowing the businesses to be used as case studies within a Sustainable Business module. The university assists the business in collating its carbon data, and the students then evaluate their operations in regard to their carbon footprint and suggest possible carbon reduction strategies that could be implemented. This partnership allows local businesses, such as this year's charity participant Love Amelia, to increase their carbon reduction capabilities, whilst also benefitting student's education and increasing their knowledge of carbon footprints, reduction methods and sustainable business.

La Empresa de Energía de Pereira (EEP), una entidad de capital 100% público , se ha unido a la Alianza Sector Eléctrico Carbono Neutral, con el objetivo de lograr la neutralidad de carbono para 2050.   

Un ejemplo destacado de colaboración con la sociedad civil es la creación de la 'Comunidad Energética Educativa' en 29 instituciones de la ciudad, una iniciativa que busca promover el acceso a energías limpias y que podría reducir 104 toneladas de CO2e al año.

column17: Reconhecendo a importância da tomada de decisão baseada em evidências para concretizar a visão do planeta de uma cidade, o município de Guimarães criou, em 2014, o inovador Laboratório da Paisagem (LP), colocando o conhecimento, a ciência e a tecnologia na vanguarda da gestão ambiental.O LP é um I&D e Educação Ambiental, e um consórcio entre o Município de Guimarães e duas das mais importantes universidades da região norte - a Universidade do Minho e a Universidade de Trás-os-Montes e Alto Douro.O LP atua de forma multidisciplinar, reunindo diferentes áreas de I&D - Biodiversidade, Espaços Verdes, Recursos Hídricos, Economia Circular e Paisagem, apoiando o município em todas as decisões.É um conceito inovador que pretende reforçar a importância do investimento das cidades em I&D+i, criando soluções que as possam tornar cada vez mais adaptadas às exigências do futuro e melhorar a qualidade de vida dos cidadãos.Na verdade, um grande catalisador para chegar aos alunos tem sido o LL, um projeto de aventura que é o símbolo e o centro da educação ambiental - através de um programa municipal de educação ambiental - PEGADAS - e um espaço de descoberta, ensino e aprendizagem.O LP conta com uma equipa totalmente empenhada, com diferentes competências científicas e elevada experiência em abordagens de ciência cidadã. LP desenvolve e gerencia vários projetos de P&D, e também é co-presidente do Grupo de Trabalho de Áreas Verdes e Biodiversidade da Rede Europeia EUROCITIES.A sustentabilidade financeira é assegurada por fundos internos do Município e por programas nacionais e europeus financiados. Ao longo dos anos, a LP criou um ambiente que estimula empregos verdes e crescimento verde (orçamento anual aumentado de € 75 mil para € 1 milhão).O LP já se revelou capaz de implementar um sistema integrado de gestão ambiental local, apostando em projetos inovadores, multidisciplinares e inclusivos, facilmente replicáveis em qualquer contexto territorial.(Fonte: Guimarães' candidacy for European Green Capital, Cycle 2025)

column17: A Iniciativa Nacional Cidades Circulares (InC2) é um programa do Ministério do Ambiente e da Ação Climática gerido pela Direção-Geral do Território, orientado para apoiar e capacitar os municípios e as suas comunidades na transição para a economia circular. A InC2 visa contribuir para melhorar as condições presentes e futuras das práticas de planeamento participativo de base local e de aprendizagem em rede para a economia circular através do apoio a redes nacionais de cidades circulares em torno de quatro temas prioritários e da capitalização nacional dos seus resultados.O apoio da InC2 às redes de cidades circulares inclui financiamento e suporte técnico e metodológico para o desenvolvimento de planos locais de ação para a economia circular e para processos de aprendizagem coletiva e partilha do conhecimento entre municípios em matéria de economia circular e desenvolvimento urbano sustentável. A metodologia inspira-se no Programa Europeu URBACT e na aplicação ao contexto nacional de décadas de experiência acumulada em redes europeias de planeamento local de ação por este programa. A InC2 concretiza um dos temas da convergência regional e nacional do Plano de Ação para a Economia Circular em Portugal - Liderar a Transição, e implementa o Programa Nacional da Política de Ordenamento do Território, contribuindo para as suas Medidas 3.11, 5.6 e 5.7.A InC2 é financiada pelo Fundo Ambiental, no quadro do objetivo “Transição para uma economia circular”, com uma dotação de 1,5 milhões de euros até 2023. A maioria do financiamento (70%) destina-se ao apoio técnico, metodológico e financeiro às redes de cidades circulares, sendo o remanescente (30%) distribuído em ações de comunicação, capitalização e na assistência técnica.https://cidadescirculares.dgterritorio.gov.pt/pages/rede-rurbanlink

column17: A iniciativa Guimarães Marca recorre a uma estratégia mercadológica territorial, afirmando-se e promovendo os vetores económicos, ambientais e culturais da cidade de Guimarães, a um nível nacional e internacional, através de uma comunidade económica vibrante e competitiva aliada ao desenvolvimento de uma identidade ímpar, o selo “Guimarães Marca”.https://marca.guimaraes.pt/Projetos associados:. I9InIniciativa que visa monitorizar projetos já implementados e promover estratégias inovadoras para a transição digital das empresas vimaranenses em áreas como a indústria 4.0, robotização, internet das coisas e sensorização. O projeto assenta no modelo de inovação que promove um conjunto de interações entre academia, indústria e o Município de Guimarães para promover o desenvolvimento económico de forma a colmatar as necessidades das empresas Guimarães Marca.. BisarA partir do projeto FromGranny To Trendy, é criada uma nova identidade visual ramificada da imagem Guimarães Marca, que visa ser comercializada e internacionalizada, tendo como conceito o upcycling através da reutilização de desperdícios industriais.As “madrinhas” - KattyXiomara, Nieta Atelier e Pé de Chumbo, responsáveis pela área criativa, terão coleções da marca dedicadas a cada uma (bisar by...).Bisar já tem ao seu lado empresas Guimarães Marca que aceitaram colaborar com o projeto. Através da doação de desperdícios industriais por parte de casa empresa, consegue-se construir uma marca focada nos seus valores e objetivos, sendo estes essenciais para a evolução da mesma.. Guimarães Circular I Mercado Valoriza+Criação de um sistema de economia circular no desenvolvimento e comercialização de produtos sustentáveis, tendo como base a estrutura industrial, científica e tecnológica de Guimarães.Será explorada uma abordagem sustentável, promovendo a utilização dos seus recursos numa ótica de desperdício zero, através de uma estratégia de pensamento colaborativo e participativo com base no Design circular e partindo da estrutura “Guimarães Marca”. Pretende-se assim desencorajar os comportamentos individuais empresariais que colocam em risco a transição para a EC, como o envio de resíduos para aterro e incineração, promovendo, por outro lado, o seu crescimento económico alavancado em novas oportunidades e ideias de negócio.Ainda, pretende-se disponibilizar uma plataforma digital que facilite o processo de criação de simbioses industriais, e que pretende focar em duas frentes distintas:Mercado online aberto B2B para resíduos industriais, repositório de informação relevante e facilitadora ao processo e espaço networking (rede social);Marketplace B2C com produtos provenientes do processo de simbiose industrial.. ICLEI is currently the largest city-level organization for cooperation between local governments and the United Nations. Since joining ICLEI in 2015, New Taipei City has actively participated in related conferences and activities.

From June 18 to 21, 2024, the ICLEI World Congress was held in São Paulo, Brazil. Deputy Mayor Liu He-Ran represented Taiwan and attended as a member of the ICLEI East Asia Executive Committee. He signed the 'ICLEI São Paulo Strategic Vision 2024-2030,' declaring New Taipei's commitment to sustainable, resilient, and inclusive urban development. Deputy Mayor Liu also shared New Taipei's experiences in climate adaptation and net-zero resilience under the “Sustainable New Taipei” vision, including strategies such as smart disaster prevention, permeable and water-retentive infrastructure, and urban core cooling measures to enhance urban resilience. ICLEI Secretary General Gino Van Begin, as well as executive committee members from Seoul, Gyeonggi Province (South Korea), Kyoto (Japan), and Changchun (China), affirmed and praised New Taipei's determination and proactive approach to addressing the potential impacts of climate change.

During the Congress, Deputy Mayor Liu also exchanged experiences on urban governance and climate action with city representatives from around the world. On the third day of the event (June 20), he met with Ms. Irene Galindo Román, Vice Mayor of Los Cabos, Mexico, who also serves as an ICLEI Global Executive Committee member for Resilience and Risk Governance. Liu shared New Taipei's experience in implementing localized action through disaster preparedness training and community disaster response capacity building.

New Taipei City has proactively addressed climate change mitigation and adaptation. Since the release of the 'New Taipei City 2050 Net-Zero Pathway and Climate Action White Paper' in 2022, the city has continuously enhanced its urban resilience. These achievements were unanimously recognized by ICLEI East Asia Executive Committee cities. As a result, Deputy Mayor Liu He-Ran was nominated to serve as the ICLEI East Asia Executive Committee Member for the “Climate Adaptation and Urban Resilience” portfolio for the 2024-2027 term.

During his term, New Taipei will continue to promote mitigation and adaptation work through its cross-sectoral “New Taipei City Climate Change Response Steering Groups.” Externally, the city will also contribute to international environmental issues in line with global trends, including climate mitigation and adaptation, coal phase-out, resilience building, and low-carbon city development. Furthermore, New Taipei is committed to sharing its successful case studies with other ICLEI member cities to collectively advance climate policy.

To encourage the transition from coal-fired boilers to gas-fired boilers, the New Taipei City Government provides a subsidy of NT$500,000 per boiler and installs natural gas pipelines to accelerate industrial transformation within the city. In recent years, growing public awareness of environmental protection has led to strong support for the phase-out of coal. Industries have also recognized the importance of environmental responsibility and are willing to cooperate. The public sector is promoting environmental justice by implementing feasible control technologies and offering financial incentives.

The city has ceased issuing new coal-use permits, and all coal-fired boilers were fully decommissioned by 2020. Existing permits were valid only until December 31, 2019. Subsidies were granted to permit holders for replacing coal-fired equipment with natural gas systems. For asphalt concrete manufacturers holding stationary pollution source permits within the city, subsidies were also provided to cover the construction costs of natural gas pipelines. Of the ten regulated asphalt plants, nine have completed the installation of natural gas pipelines.

The city also provides guidance based on registered emissions source data and continues to track their subsequent reduction measures.

According to New Taipei City's greenhouse gas inventory analysis, emissions from the building sector account for approximately 40% of the city's total greenhouse gas emissions. In response, the city launched the New Taipei Energy-Saving E-House Program in 2022. The “E” stands for “energy efficiency,” promoting energy-efficient residential buildings. The program introduces an energy efficiency rating system based on the Energy Use Intensity (EUI) of common-area facilities. Partnering with real estate agencies, the city publishes lists of high-efficiency communities on property listing platforms, enabling prospective buyers or tenants to assess the electricity performance of buildings during housing selection.

Under this program, EUI is used to evaluate energy consumption in public areas, with lower EUI values indicating better performance. Communities are rated from three to six stars based on their EUI scores, with higher ratings representing better energy efficiency. This rating system fosters a sense of pride among residents, encourages recognition of low-carbon practices, and motivates neighboring communities to join the E-House initiative, thus cultivating a grassroots energy-saving culture.

The program enhances public understanding of community-level energy use and adds new criteria for property decision-making—much like the introduction of energy labels for home appliances, which have influenced consumer behavior. As of the end of 2024, a total of 442 communities in New Taipei City have participated in the E-House Program.

Additionally, the city provides technical consultation and support, including site assessments by expert teams known as “Power-Saving Clinics,” guidance from certified “Low-Carbon Community Planners,” and access to resources under the “Low-Carbon Community Retrofit” scheme. These services help identify major energy-consuming systems and support low-carbon upgrades for public facilities. Through joint efforts from businesses, residents, and the government, New Taipei City is gradually transforming private buildings into near-zero-carbon buildings, contributing to the long-term goal of becoming a net-zero carbon city.
