La Municipalidad de Godoy Cruz promueve múltiples espacios de trabajo conjunto entre distintos actores.

Con el sector privado, el programa Empresas Sostenibles fomenta la cooperación en materia de sostenibilidad y cambio climático. A través de este programa, las empresas pueden obtener una certificación en sostenibilidad, reportando sus acciones en los ámbitos ambiental, económico y de gobernanza. Además, el programa impulsa la implementación de prácticas de responsabilidad social empresarial, la realización de capacitaciones y el desarrollo de proyectos conjuntos orientados a la mejora continua en materia ambiental.

Con la academia y las instituciones educativas, se promueve el intercambio de conocimiento mediante consultas interdisciplinarias y el diseño de proyectos específicos, orientados a la innovación en sostenibilidad y gestión climática.

En relación con la sociedad civil, el municipio participa activamente en redes y organizaciones que promueven la acción climática y el desarrollo sostenible, tales como la Red Argentina de Municipios frente al Cambio Climático (RAMCC), RIL, CIPPEC, ICLEI, entre otras. Estas alianzas permiten compartir buenas prácticas, acceder a capacitación técnica y fortalecer la gestión local del cambio climático a través de la cooperación interinstitucional. Por otro lado, para la reducción de residuos, se trabaja con cooperativas de recuperadores urbanos para la gestión de los residuos secos, como también con el Banco de Alimentos, para evitar la pérdida y desperdicio de alimentos.
Desde 2017, Godoy Cruz mantiene una alianza con ONU-Hábitat, orientada al desarrollo urbano sostenible y a la promoción de principios como la inclusión social, la igualdad de género, la sostenibilidad ambiental y la resiliencia. 
A nivel interjurisdiccional, el municipio coordina acciones con otros gobiernos locales del Área Metropolitana de Mendoza. Un ejemplo destacado es la Red Metropolitana de Ciclovías, desarrollada de manera conjunta para conectar las trazas de los distintos departamentos y fomentar así el uso del transporte activo y sostenible por parte de la población. De igual modo, se articulan políticas comunes en gestión integral de residuos y transporte público urbano —como el Metrotranvía y las líneas de colectivos—, buscando mejorar la eficiencia del sistema y reducir las emisiones de gases de efecto invernadero.
Por último, la Municipalidad realiza revisiones técnicas de los dictámenes de evaluación ambiental vinculados a obras públicas y privadas, con el fin de analizar sus impactos ambientales potenciales y definir medidas de mitigación o reversión de los efectos negativos. Este proceso refuerza la gestión preventiva y promueve un desarrollo urbano más sostenible y responsable con el entorno.

Colaboración en Reforestación

La Dirección Municipal de Medio Ambiente impulsó jornadas de plantación de árboles en espacios escolares, parques y áreas públicas, donde participaron estudiantes de primaria, secundaria y preparatoria.

Se buscó fomentar la cultura de cuidado del arbolado desde la niñez, explicando la importancia de los árboles en la captación de agua, mejora de la calidad del aire y regulación del clima urbano.

Estas actividades se diseñaron como ejercicios prácticos de aprendizaje, en los que los alumnos no solo plantaron, sino también aprendieron sobre el mantenimiento de los árboles (riego, poda adecuada y protección).


Pláticas y Educación Ambiental

Se realizaron charlas en aulas y auditorios sobre:

Cambio climático y sus impactos locales.

Manejo adecuado de residuos y reciclaje.

Importancia de la biodiversidad urbana y las áreas verdes.

Estas pláticas buscaron sensibilizar a los jóvenes sobre su papel como agentes de cambio, resaltando la relación entre sus hábitos cotidianos y la salud ambiental de la ciudad.

Catbalogan City works closely with the National Government through multiple agencies such as the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR), Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH), Department of Agriculture (DA), Department of Energy (DOE), Department of Health (DOH), and Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD). These collaborations involve technical assistance, capacity building, and funding support for local adaptation and mitigation projects. Examples include DENR's partnership on reforestation and mangrove rehabilitation under the WOW Antiao Ridge-to-Reef Program, DPWH's investments in resilient infrastructure and flood control systems, and DOE's programs promoting renewable energy and energy efficiency in government facilities.

The city also benefits from national grants such as the People's Survival Fund (PSF) for climate adaptation planning and implementation, and partnerships through the Climate Change Commission for aligning the Local Climate Change Action Plan (LCCAP) with national priorities. Collaborative efforts have led to improved access to climate data, technical expertise for risk mapping, and increased integration of disaster risk reduction in land use planning.

Progress is evident in the institutionalization of Catbalogan's CLUP and LCCAP, enhanced disaster preparedness programs, and incremental implementation of renewable energy and sustainable agriculture initiatives. These partnerships ensure that national policies are localized, while Catbalogan's specific vulnerabilities and strengths are addressed in planning and project delivery.

Kota Jambi telah melaksanakan inisiatif 'Bangkit Berdaya' (Bangun Kelurahan Secara Intensif dan Terpadu yang Berasaskan Swadaya Masyarakat) sejak tahun 2014. Inisiatif ini bertujuan untuk mempercepat pembangunan infrastruktur di tingkat lokal/komunitas, dimana masyarakat dapat mengusulkan kegiatan yang kemudian ditindaklanjuti oleh dinas terkait di lingkungan Pemerintah Kota. Setiap usulan diverifikasi terlebih dahulu oleh dinas terkait sebelum disetujui, setelah itu Pemerintah Kota melakukan pengadaan barang dan jasa sesuai kebutuhan masyarakat.

Capaian utama dari inisiatif ini antara lain:
- Pembangunan jalan baru sepanjang 192.840 meter
- Pembangunan drainase baru sepanjang 33.516 meter
- 58 unit sumur umum
- 37 unit tangki septik komunal
- 16 unit toilet umum
- 24 unit posyandu (fasilitas kesehatan terpadu untuk bayi dan balita)

Program ini memungkinkan Pemerintah kota untuk memanfaatkan anggaran se-efisien mungkin. Sebagai gambaran, pada tahun 2022, jumlah dana yang dialokasikan untuk proyek ini sebesar Rp 43.075.482.372. Jika seluruh anggaran tersebut hanya digunakan untuk pembangunan jalan, maka kota hanya dapat membangun jalan sepanjang 28.717 meter. Namun, dengan melibatkan masyarakat melalui inisiatif ini, jumlah anggaran yang sama mampu menghasilkan pembangunan jalan sepanjang 192.840 meter.

Inisiatif ini juga telah mendapatkan pengakuan internasional. column17: Miami-Dade County has piloted an approach called \'Adaptation Action Areas\' (AAA) to promote resident engagement around critical climate issues, particular related to Sea Level Rise and Flooding. This approach was first identified in 2011 when the Florida Legislature created Adaptation Action Areas (S.163.3177 Florida Statutes). This statutory policy tool which is an optional designation within the Coastal Management Element is defined as:“'Adaptation Action Area' or 'Adaptation Area' means a designation in the coastal management element of a local government's comprehensive plan which identifies one or more areas that experience coastal flooding due to extreme high tides and storm surge, and that are vulnerable to the related impacts of rising sea levels for the purpose of prioritizing funding for infrastructure needs and adaptation planning”Our pilot AAA was located in the \'Little River\' area, a part of Miami-Dade County that is very prone to flooding during heavy rainfall events and king tides . This often causes drainage systems and septic tanks to fail, and leads to the backup of sewage into homes and waterways, with significant financial, health and other consequences. These issues also overlap with other climate hazards such as extreme heat and pollution.The Little River AAA planning project has three primary goals, which are to:• Align relevant studies, data, and planned projects• Collaborate with community members to identify values, challenges, projects, andpolicies to adapt to sea level rise• Develop a forward-looking adaptation plan that includes next steps, policy changes,and ongoing and planned projectsThe planning process has brought together many key stakeholders who may otherwise work in silos in order to stitch a more complete picture of the needs and possible short- and long-term solutions.Residents, County and city staff and other partners have learned a tremendous amount about not just the array of challenges in the Little River AAA, but also about what it takes to coordinate across disciplines and jurisdictions in support of an equitable adaptation planning effort. This AAA planning effort builds on years of studies and guidance developed by the Florida Department of Environmental Protection and draws from the experience of other local governments exploring AAAs as a flexible local-level planning tool. This work also supports direct implementation of the County's Thrive 305 Action Plan.This effort has been a success in engagement, and has involved extensive outreach, workshops, local meetings, and other interactive activities to advance climate action and equity in the area.

column17:
1. Kerja Sama dengan Gemawan

Pemkot lewat BAPPERIDA bekerja sama dengan Gemawan, sebuah lembaga masyarakat sipil lokal, melalui program Pontianak Tangguh Iklim, berkolaborasi dengan berbagai pemangku kepentingan — termasuk universitas melalui riset RISE (Resilient Indonesian Slums Envisioned) dan organisasi seperti Hivos dan KotaKita. Riset ini fokus pada tiga isu utama: banjir rob, sampah, dan energi, terutama dengan perhatian khusus pada kondisi wilayah kumuh kota. Diseminasi hasil riset ini bertujuan agar temuan menjadi dasar implementasi kebijakan yang inklusif; seperti peningkatan pengelolaan air hujan, sanitasi, dan akses layanan bagi masyarakat rentan. Upaya ini menegaskan bahwa pendekatan iklim tidak hanya teknis, tetapi juga sosial — menempatkan kesejahteraan dan ketahanan warga miskin sebagai pusat perencanaan aksi iklim.

2. Kerja Sama dengan Proyek FINCAPES

Pemkot Pontianak, melalui BAPPERIDA, menjalin kerja sama dengan proyek FINCAPES (Flood Impacts, Carbon Pricing, and Ecosystem Sustainability) yang dipimpin oleh University of Waterloo, Kanada. Kolaborasi ini mencakup riset teknis bersama Fakultas Teknik Universitas Syiah Kuala untuk mengembangkan skenario ancaman banjir rob di Pontianak. Tujuan utamanya adalah menyajikan data dan pemetaan risiko banjir dan telahtuli digunakan sebagai landasan dalam perencanaan mitigasi berbasis bukti, memperkuat kebijakan pemerintah daerah, termasuk dalam penyusunan dan implementasi RPJMD 2025-2029. Hasil penelitian ini diharapkan membantu pemerintah merumuskan kebijakan adaptasi dan investasi infrastruktur yang lebih tepat, serta meningkatkan kesiapsiagaan kota terhadap dampak perubahan iklim.

3. Kerja sama pembangunan SPALDT

Pembangunan SPALD-T (Sistem Pengelolaan Air Limbah Domestik Terpusat) di Pontianak merupakan hasil kolaborasi erat antara Pemerintah Kota, Kementerian PUPR, dan Asian Development Bank (ADB) melalui program Citywide Inclusive Sanitation Project (CISP). Dengan alokasi pendanaan mencapai sekitar Rp1,5 triliun, proyek ini menargetkan 35 persen penduduk kota dapat terlayani oleh sistem terpusat, sementara sisanya dilayani sistem setempat (on-site). Sejak pertengahan 2025, pemerintah daerah telah menyelesaikan kriteria kesiapan (readiness criteria), termasuk penentuan lahan di Nipah Kuning dan Martapura, penyelesaian akses jalan dengan Pelindo, hingga pembukaan lelang paket fisik. Mobilisasi kontraktor direncanakan sebelum akhir 2025, sehingga SPALD-T dapat segera beroperasi sebagai solusi jangka panjang untuk pengelolaan limbah domestik yang ramah lingkungan dan berkontribusi pada penurunan emisi karbon.

4. Kerja sama revitalisasi TPA Batulayang 

Proyek ini mendapat dukungan besar dari pemerintah pusat dengan kucuran dana Rp260 miliar melalui skema reimbursement. Proyek ini bertujuan mengubah TPA menjadi sanitary landfill modern yang lebih ramah lingkungan dan mampu mengurangi risiko pencemaran. Revitalisasi ini juga diintegrasikan dengan pembangunan Tempat Pengolahan Sampah Terpadu (TPST) yang mampu mengolah hingga 400 ton sampah per hari. Selain dana dari pusat, Pontianak juga memperoleh dukungan Bank Dunia sebesar Rp205 miliar untuk membangun pabrik pengolahan sampah, termasuk produksi kompos, pemanfaatan gas metana, serta pengolahan sampah plastik menjadi bahan bangunan atau bahan bakar alternatif. Dengan langkah ini, pengelolaan sampah di Pontianak diarahkan tidak hanya untuk mengurangi timbunan, tetapi juga menciptakan nilai tambah ekonomi sirkular yang inklusif.

5. Kerja sama proyek Konfersi Terang

Proyek ini merupakan usulan dari Pemkot Pontianak untuk mendapatkan pendanaan dari mitra GCOM. Bentuknya dengan mengubah seluruh lampu penerangan jalan dan ruang publik, serta trafic light menjadi lampu yang lebih ramah lingkungan. Saat ini sudah dilakukan penandatangan kerja sama terbaru untuk pendampingan, namun masih menunggu tindak lanjut dari GCoM.

Title of collaboration:
Integrated and Participatory Climate Action for Kadıköy Municipality

Partners:
Turkey Europe Foundation

Kadıköy City Council

Civil society organizations (e.g. Greenpeace, TMMOB Chambers, local NGOs)

Academia (e.g. Marmara University, Istanbul Technical University, Yıldız Technical University)

Private sector (e.g. Energon, Froniss Istanbul, RKT Energy)

Type of collaboration:
Multi-stakeholder partnership on climate adaptation, mitigation, and public engagement.

Description & Progress:
This collaboration was launched to design and implement Kadıköy's Sustainable Energy and Climate Action Plan (SECAP) and Climate Adaptation Plan. It included workshops, public consultations, and technical input from universities, private companies, and NGOs. Key achievements include:

A 40% emission reduction target by 2030;

Climate vulnerability analysis and green corridor planning;

Public awareness campaigns and community-based programs;

A monitoring framework with over 40 performance indicators.

This collaborative process built local ownership of climate goals and improved the technical quality and legitimacy of the plans. It remains active through annual reviews and stakeholder events.

Timeframe:
2017 - ongoing

Impact:
Enhanced cross-sectoral coordination;

Better access to funding (e.g., EU IPA);

Stronger public support and inclusion in climate policy.

A Prefeitura de Francisco Morato vem consolidando sua participação em diferentes plataformas de reporte e monitoramento de dados, o que tem permitido avanços significativos na gestão pública e no fortalecimento das políticas de sustentabilidade.

No âmbito do IBGE, o município tem seus principais indicadores sociais, econômicos e demográficos constantemente atualizados, o que possibilita diagnósticos mais precisos e fundamenta a formulação de programas voltados à melhoria da qualidade de vida da população.

Com a adesão ao ICLEI - Governos Locais pela Sustentabilidade, Francisco Morato passou a integrar uma rede internacional de cidades comprometidas com a ação climática. A partir dessa colaboração, o município desenvolveu iniciativas como a Assembleia Cidadã pelo Clima e o Relatório Local Voluntário da Agenda 2030, que reforçam a participação social, a transparência e o alinhamento com os Objetivos de Desenvolvimento Sustentável (ODS).

Embora ainda em fase de estruturação, o engajamento junto a plataformas como o CDP (Carbon Disclosure Project) representa a intenção de ampliar a mensuração e a divulgação de dados climáticos, criando condições para captar investimentos, estabelecer parcerias técnicas e adotar práticas de mitigação e adaptação às mudanças climáticas.

Adicionalmente, a busca por indicadores de eficiência administrativa, como o IGEM, contribui para a avaliação da governança local, sinalizando áreas que necessitam de aprimoramento e estimulando boas práticas de gestão pública.

Essas colaborações já resultam em maior integração entre planejamento urbano e políticas ambientais, além de promoverem o fortalecimento institucional da Prefeitura. O município avança, assim, no caminho de se tornar mais resiliente, sustentável e transparente, construindo uma agenda pública alinhada às demandas locais e aos compromissos globais.

São exemplo o projeto SPARCS (Sustainable energy Positive & zero cARbon CommunitieS) que visa demonstrar e validar soluções inovadoras e replicáveis com vista à obtenção de sistemas energéticos positivos, inteligentes e integrados, tendo por base o envolvimento e participação ativa da comunidade. 
Outro projeto é o EHHUR (EYES HEARTS HANDS - Urban Revolution) visa desenvolver e testar uma metodologia disruptiva e integrada direcionada para a transformação do ambiente construído (materiais, produtos, edifícios, espaços públicos, infraestruturas, redes de serviços), assente em boas práticas já existentes a nível europeu, complementando-as com os princípios orientadores do Novo Bauhaus Europeu (NEB).
A Maia integra também diferentes redes europeias e internacionais de partilha de boas práticas e conhecimento, de que são exemplo a adesão ao Pacto dos Autarcas em 2017.

Pacto dos Autarcas - O Município da Maia subscreveu em 2017 o Pacto de Autarcas para o Clima e Energia. Esta iniciativa reúne autoridades locais e regionais europeias para que intensifiquem a ação na luta contra as alterações climáticas e na busca por soluções energéticas sustentáveis, através do incentivo ao desenvolvimento de planos, promoção de ações e partilha de conhecimento. 
Rede Cidades pelo Clima - O Município da Maia faz parte desde 2024 desta rede cujo objetivo é acelerar a transição para a neutralidade climática das cidades e regiões portuguesas, em alinhamento com a Missão Europeia “100 cidades climaticamente neutras e inteligentes até 2030, por e para os cidadãos”. 
RAISE-PT - Esta iniciativa baseia-se numa comunidade colaborativa permanente focada na transição energética com vista à discussão contínua, à promoção de soluções criativas e inovadoras, bem como à melhoria do quadro político para gerar investimentos em projetos de eficiência energética e energia sustentável. 
BaZe - O incentivo da Câmara Municipal da Maia aos seus munícipes para a adoção de comportamentos sustentáveis tem sido feito sobretudo através do projeto BaZe. Em 2019, o processo de Cocriação iniciou-se com a proposta de trabalhar a cultura colaborativa. Este é um exemplo de colaboração do Município com a comunidade local.

column17: A Rede Cidades pelo Clima é uma iniciativa colaborativa, sem personalidade jurídica, que tem por missão acelerar a transição para a neutralidade climática das cidades e regiões portuguesas, em alinhamento com a Missão Europeia “100 cidades climaticamente neutras e inteligentes até 2030, por e para os cidadãos”. \nA Rede Cidades pelo Clima foi fundada pelas cidades e regiões portuguesas que manifestaram o seu interesse em integrar a Missão Europeia e desenvolver um processo conducente à assinatura de um “Contrato Climático para a Cidade”, incorporando uma estratégia e um plano de ação para a neutralidade climática em 2030. \nO Município da Figueira da Foz aderiu a esta Rede em Fevereiro de 2023 e encontra-se inserido nos 4 Grupos de Trabalho criados para o efeito: Energia, Mobilidade, Edifícios e Mecanismos de Sequestro de Carbono. O objetivo da Rede é apoiar os municípios essencialmente na preparação de projetos inerentes à mitigação, assim como pressionar de alguma forma o governo central para a disponibilização de fontes de financiamento para a implementação de projetos que se enquadrem num dos Grupos de Trabalho definidos.

column17: Rede “CAPT2 - Circularidade da Água: Por todos e Para Todos”No âmbito da Iniciativa Nacional Cidades Circulares (InC2) , promovida pela Direção Geral do Território (DGT) do Ministério do Ambiente e da Ação Climática, que visou apoiar e capacitar os municípios e suas comunidades para a transição para uma economia mais circular e para um desenvolvimento urbano mais sustentável, através da constituição e funcionamento de Redes de Cidades Circulares (RC2), o município de Loulé integrou, em março de 2021, uma candidatura conjunta com outros municípios (com diferentes características, segundo critérios previamente estabelecidos), ao eixo temático “Ciclo Urbano da Água”, candidatura que foi selecionada para implementação. Neste enquadramento, foi constituída a Rede “CAPT2 - Circularidade da Água: Por todos e Para Todos”, parceria liderada pelo Laboratório da Paisagem (Guimarães), que envolveu os municípios de Águeda, Lagoa (Açores), Loulé, Mértola, Oeiras, Oliveira de Frades e Ponte de Sor, e que tem como objetivos:•Promover a integração da reutilização de água no planeamento e gestão dos recursos hídricos;•Incentivar à adoção das melhores práticas, através do apoio à inovação e investimento e desenvolvimento de ações que promovam a transição para uma economia circular;•Potenciar a gestão integrada, eficaz e participativa do Ciclo Urbano da Água.Após finalização da primeira fase (em dezembro de 2021), que culminou com a elaboração de um Estudo Base, o projeto da rede CAPT2 iniciou, em fevereiro de 2022, a Fase 2, que teve a duração de 16 meses. Esta Fase 2 resultou então no desenvolvimento dos Planos Locais de Ação Integrada (PLAI) adaptados a cada município, instrumentos que se pretende que contribuam para a melhoria do desenho de estratégias urbanas sustentáveis na transição para uma economia circular, tendo por base um processo de planeamento de ação plenamente colaborativo e cocriador, assente num modelo de governança participativo.

Nas eleições dos órgãos sociais, ocorridas em setembro de 2022, o presidente da Câmara Municipal de Loulé, Vítor Aleixo, foi eleito presidente da direção da adapt.local.A adapt.local assume como missão promover um processo contínuo de planeamento adaptativo que aumente a capacidade dos municípios portugueses e de outras entidades, públicas ou privadas, em incorporar a adaptação às alterações climáticas nas suas políticas de atuação e nos seus instrumentos, afirmando a importância da escala local para a conceção e implementação de soluções de adaptação mais eficazes, eficientes e equitativas.

O Município de Loulé integra a Rede de Cidades e Vilas que Caminham.
A Câmara Municipal de Loulé aderiu formalmente à Rede de Cidades e Vilas que Caminham, através de um protocolo celebrado com o Instituto de Cidades e Vilas com Mobilidade (ICVM), no dia 14 de dezembro de 2023.

A bandeira da rede foi hasteada nos Paços do Concelho e passa a ser, a partir de agora, o símbolo da aposta da Autarquia em que cada vez mais cidadãos andem a pé pela cidade, optando pelo caminhar em detrimento do uso do carro. Há diversas mais-valias neste projeto, que vão da melhoria da saúde pública dos habitantes à economia de proximidade que beneficiará o comércio local. Mas também o fortalecimento da sociabilização no espaço público, por exemplo com o regresso do “caminho da escola”, a acessibilidades para todos os cidadãos, a “amigabilidade” da cidade e dos lugares urbanos e, naturalmente, o contributo para a mitigação das alterações climáticas.

Esta rede portuguesa foi criada com o objetivo de estabelecer uma plataforma de partilha de experiências e de soluções que constituem excelentes exemplos de boas práticas urbanas em matéria de mobilidade sustentável, suave e ativa.

É um projeto que pretende garantir, aos municípios integrantes, o desenvolvimento de trabalhos para uma cidade mais qualificada e inclusiva, onde o andar a pé se pretende tornar como o mais importante modo de deslocação.

O Município de Loulé foi convidado para integrar o consórcio europeu do projeto AGE-X-HEAT, que se encontra a preparar uma candidatura ao programa HORIZON-MISS-2025-01-CLIMA-04 - Testing and demonstrating innovative solutions to improve resilience to extreme heat, including addressing health impacts (Testar e demonstrar soluções inovadoras para melhorar a resiliência ao calor extremo, incluindo a abordagem dos impactos na saúde).
O consórcio internacional inclui a Organização Mundial de Saúde, a Faculdade de Engenharia da Universidade do Porto, o Instituto do Ambiente da Finlândia, o Instituto da Habitação e Ambiente da Alemanha e o BC3 - Centro para as Alterações Climáticas do País Basco, entidades que irão definir e desenhar as soluções. Para além das entidades referidas, o consórcio inclui ainda 4+4 cidades de quatro países, nomeadamente: Tampere e Lathi (Finlândia), Hamburg e Bad Nauheim (Alemanha), Porto e Loulé (Portugal) e Bilbao Vitoria-Gasteiz (País Basco), autoridades locais que terão como papel demonstrar e replicar as soluções propostas para resposta de adaptação a eventos de calor extremo no ambiente construído, com especial ênfase no envelhecimento da população.
De acordo com o definido na call de candidatura, as soluções devem dar resposta a:
• Desenvolver, demonstrar e avaliar medidas sistémicas para reduzir e gerir o stress térmico nos espaços públicos e privados e no ambiente construído, evitando, ao mesmo tempo, a “má adaptação”;
• Desenvolver e demonstrar ações prontas a utilizar para os serviços de emergência, transporte público, etc., em caso de eventos de calor extremo, bem como apoiar o planeamento de preparação e prevenção de catástrofes.
• Explorar e avaliar opções de financiamento inovadores para implementar as soluções de resiliência térmica propostas para regiões/autoridades locais, que operam em diferentes contextos (por exemplo, jurisdição, governação e partes interessadas, etc.).
Como autoridade local, é esperado do município de Loulé uma estreita colaboração no desenvolvimento e melhoria de processos de planeamento, ações preparatórias e intervenções que visam reduzir o efeito do calor extremo entre a população idosa. Neste contexto, e enquanto cidade/concelho replicador, “O município de Loulé pretende adaptar/desenvolver, implementar e testar soluções que possam aumentar a resiliência da sua população idosa ao calor extremo e às ondas de calor.”
As medidas propostas pelo município de Loulé para incorporação na candidatura estão alinhadas com os seguintes eixos (AL) e foram as seguintes:
AL1 - Diagnóstico Local e Identificação de Idosos Vulneráveis
• Desenvolvimento de um 'mapa de calor' da temperatura da cidade de Loulé | RESULTADO 1: Mapa de Calor e identificação de hotspots;
• Inquérito aos idosos mais vulneráveis (i.e., em risco de exclusão social e/ou isolamento) através da compilação e cruzamento de bases de dados municipais existentes (por exemplo, proteção civil, serviços sociais, etc.) | RESULTADO 2: Lista dos idosos mais vulneráveis.
AL2 - Rede Piloto de Abrigos Climáticos Acessíveis
• Levantamento e mapeamento de locais existentes adequados para utilização como abrigos climáticos acessíveis durante períodos de calor extremo/prolongado | RESULTADO 3: Lista e mapa dos locais referidos;
• Identificação de dois edifícios ou infraestruturas municipais existentes para utilização como abrigos de refrigeração acessíveis em caso de períodos de calor extremo/prolongado; Avaliação dos requisitos para a sua adaptação (por exemplo, climatização, zonas de estar, dispensadores de água, etc.) e implementação das obras necessárias | RESULTADO 4: Dois abrigos de refrigeração acessíveis;
• Avaliação dos requisitos para a adaptação de espaços públicos exteriores (aqueles mais frequentados pela população idosa) mais suscetíveis ao efeito de 'ilha de calor' (por exemplo, plantação de árvores para melhor sombreamento, criação de elementos de água para regulação da temperatura, etc.) | RESULTADO 5: Lista de espaços públicos e obras necessárias à sua adaptação;
• Adaptação de um dos espaços públicos exteriores acima referidos, considerado prioritário | RESULTADO 6: Um espaço público exterior adequadamente adaptado a períodos de calor extremo/prolongado.
AL3 - Sistema de Alerta Precoce e Rede de Apoio
• Desenvolvimento de um Plano/Protocolo de Contingência e de um sistema de alerta precoce, especificamente dirigido aos idosos mais vulneráveis, em caso de períodos de calor extremo/prolongado | RESULTADO 7: Plano/Protocolo de Contingência e sistema de alerta precoce.
AL4 - Combate à Pobreza Energética entre Idosos
• Aproximar os dois Balcões de Energia de Loulé (um localizado num espaço físico e o outro móvel) da população idosa, oferecendo-lhes consultoria sobre como tornar as suas casas mais resistentes às alterações climáticas e orientando-os sobre quaisquer oportunidades de financiamento disponíveis.
AL5 - Monitorização, Partilha de Informação e Divulgação

O município de Loulé integra a Rede de Cidades pelo Clima. Constituída em maio de 2024, a Rede Cidades pelo Clima é uma iniciativa colaborativa sem personalidade jurídica, fundada pelas 20 cidades e regiões portuguesas que manifestaram o seu interesse em integrar a Missão Europeia '100 Cidades Climaticamente Neutras e Inteligentes até 2030'. A iniciativa surgiu do compromisso de cidades e regiões portuguesas para acelerar a transição para a neutralidade climática, está alinhada com a referida Missão Europeia e está aberta a todos os municípios e comunidades intermunicipais que partilham este objetivo.
A Rede Cidades pelo Clima integra à data os municípios de: Abrantes, Braga, Cascais, Famalicão, Figueira da Foz, Guimarães, Lisboa, Loulé, Loures, Maia, Matosinhos, Porto, Tomar, Torres Vedras, Sintra, Valongo, Viana do Castelo, Vila Franca de Xira e Vila Nova de Gaia. São ainda membros a Comunidade Intermunicipal da Região de Coimbra e a Comunidade Intermunicipal do Oeste.
De salientar que a Missão da Rede Cidades pelo Clima tem como linhas de atuação a ação e mobilização baseadas no conhecimento e a coordenação de esforços entre as cidades e regiões, as partes interessadas e a Administração Central e Regional.
Para além dos Órgãos Sociais (Assembleia Geral, Conselho Coordenador e Conselho Consultivo) e do Secretariado Técnico da Rede, as atividades da Cidades pelo Clima estão estruturadas em quatro Grupos de Trabalho que se interligam e interagem entre si, e no âmbito dos quais são desenvolvidas ações e medidas de política pública relevantes para os contratos climáticos, com enfoque em:
• Energia - Produção local de energia renovável. Iluminação pública inteligente e multifuncional;
• Edifícios - Reabilitação energética do edificado;
• Mobilidade - Infraestruturas, redes, tecnologia e alteração dos padrões de mobilidade.
• Remoção de Carbono - Soluções baseadas na natureza para a remoção de carbono
As sessões dos Grupos de Trabalho são espaços dinâmicos de interação, onde se promove a troca de informação, o esclarecimento de dúvidas e a partilha de experiências e desafios. As sessões acontecem de forma híbrida (presencial e virtual) para garantir a participação ativa de todos os envolvidos.

'An Inclusive Transition to Net Zero'

Phase 1. Understand the Challenge. Through training and support from University of York Policy Hub, a group of community researchers from underrepresented neighbourhoods in Bradford which have existing, known obstacles to net zero (e.g. high levels of fuel poverty, low-income areas) were identified to support this climate-related community research project. 

The research project started in January 2025 and will complete by December 2025.

The community researcher cohort will feed into the Council's Climate Action Plan and delivery process. The aims of the community-led research include:
1.	building local residents' skills, readiness, knowledge and awareness to participate in net zero discussions and advocate for change;
2.	delivering a series of community-based workshops to understand (evidence) the risks, opportunities and inequalities that different families and communities might face as a result of the transition to net zero; 
3.	co-producing evidence and areas of action to inform the district's Climate Action planning and delivery process, and future applications for climate-related funding.

The community workshops were co-produced with the community researcher cohort in Bradford to assist the full workshop process, including co-design of workshop materials, co-facilitation and contribute to analysis. This included participant recruitment - 16 participants in each location.

As part of the research, facilitation and data management training for community researchers, the University of York Policy Hub team took time to upskill the community and facilitate their long-term support capabilities in the climate change space. This included 'Climate Fresk' training which provided a beginner's overview of climate change science, and made relevant to the communities involved.

Phase 2. A three-part in-person workshop series were conducted in the selected neighbourhoods in Bradford during July 2025 - based around 'Understanding family and community vulnerabilities in transition to Net Zero'.

Workshop 1 focused on gaining a common understanding of net zero as a group, learning existing feelings, anxieties and climate change concerns as well as mapping community assets in their neighbourhood and Bradford generally. 

Workshop 2 focused on transitioning understanding of their community and their family into a context of net zero. 

Workshop 3 focused on Bradford's District Plan, feeding back with suggestions around personal and city level engagement and implementation for best results. This will include aspects of data for community level decision making and data visualisation for communities.

Phase 3 & 4 will take place from August - December 20205.

Phase 3. Build a vision for Just Climate Futures in the community.
University of York will bring together Bradford Council, community and relevant stakeholders in a workshop to build towards action on net zero in Bradford. The aim is to increase community trust and meaningful engagement on the Net Zero District Plan and foster collaborations that may extend beyond the duration of the research project. 

The theme of the workshop will be influenced on the outcomes of Phase 1 and 2. involving the community researchers and include activities such as problem solving of a relevant issue (e.g. transportation), creative co-production visuals, community asset and stakeholder mapping, zine-making, and creating principles for implementing the climate action plan based on optimising public benefit.

Participants will include groups/stakeholders not involved in the Climate Action Plan development - and include policy actors, local charity organisations, NGOs, faith leaders, council staff, NHS workers, teachers, employers the council procures work from, and local business owners. These groups do not need to be already involved in the climate change and net zero space.

Phase 4. Plan for Just Climate Futures in the Community (Policy and Design for Inclusion).

This involves analysis, outputs and dissemination. The community researchers will be asked if/how they would like to take part in this analysis phase, learning research skills and learning about the analysis process. Outputs will include manifestos, co-produced animation, co-produced policy brief, data visualisation, co-produced full report highlighting the project's process and findings, academic journal articles. 

A follow-up to this is a half-day worshop entitled 'Inclusive Retrofit: Sharing Solutions Workshop' . This will be delivered by University of Yorkshire in collaboration with WYCA and Bradford Council, hosted in Bradford in November 2025 and bring together policymakers, community groups, and regional actors to develop practical solutions for a fair and and inclusive approach to retrofitting buildings across Yorkshire.

Bradford Council secured funding of almost £1million from Innovate UK in 2024 and successfully led the formation and development of Bradford Manufacturing Futures (BMF) and appointed consultants to develop a district-wide industrial decarbonisation roadmap and investment prospectus.

BMF is a cross-sector partnership of nine local organisations, including established industry leaders and the University of Bradford, who have come together to develop the Local Industrial Decarbonisation Project (LIDP). 

Key stages of LIDP included stakeholder engagement, emissions analysis and site surveys to understand the manufacturing energy demands and decarbonisation intervention opportunities, such as fuel switching technology. 

The partnership provides a platform to share the responsibility and knowledge to support the transition to renewable energy sources for 30 manufacturers in some of the highest emitting sectors, including chemicals, food, basic metals, mineral products and metal fabrication, which produce 52% of the district's CO2 emissions. This includes exploring the possibilities around capturing and/or utilising CO2 emissions and repurposing heat that might otherwise be wasted.

Key achievements include:
-A district-wide industrial Decarbonisation Pathway outlining how manufacturing-related emissions could be reduced by over 90% by 2040.

-An Investment Prospectus which identifies opportunities in renewable energy and low-carbon technologies, such as heat pumps, solar PV, wind, hydrogen, and biomethane - to protect 24,000 jobs and create further employment growth.

-Creation of five geographical Clean Growth Hubs, representing over 30 manufacturers. 

-Establishment of 'Sustainability Leaders of the Future' programme to nuture tomorrow's local talent. 

Bradford is recognised by the Government's Department for Energy Security and Net Zero as one of 13 key industrial clusters in England with strategic potential for decarbonisation. 

https://www.bradfordcluster.co.uk/

Since the conclusion of LIDP and launch of BMF in February 2025, BMF is now established as a not-for-profit limited company and aims to drive clean growth in manufacturing. Its overarching goals are to:
-Be the trust voice of industry for Bradford District.
-Champion all manufacturers and share expertise 
to sustain industrial prosperity within the district.
-Through collaboration and investment, drive the transition to net zero via energy efficiency and fuel switching technology.
-Inspire the next generation of talented leaders in sustainable manufacturing. 

Now with an established BMF board, it aims to achieve its goals by attracting funding and growing its membership and developing three dedicated interest groups which will focus on energy efficiency, fuel switching and SME clean growth.

https://www.bradfordcluster.co.uk/

Following being mandated to implement a Class C Charging Clean Air Zone (CAZ) in 2020, Bradford MDC have collaborated extensively to comply with the direction and the Air Quality (England) Regulations 2010, whilst also improving health and addressing the climate emergency. Following securing the largest funding allocation in the UK for a zone of its type the CAZ was launched using in-house resources, on time and within budget on the 26th September 2022.
The Council have collaborated with Governments Joint Air Quality Unit, the Central Service at the DVLA local businesses and the public to implement the zone, also with the NHS to evaluate health improvements as a result of the CAZ. 
Health improvements from significant reductions in Nitrogen Dioxide and reductions in health inequalities (Ref NHS research - Impact of an urban city-wide Bradford clean air plan on health service use and nitrogen dioxide 24 months after implementation: An interrupted time series analysis - ScienceDirect ) saving over £30,000 month in the NHS. These being 24% and 25% reductions in cardiovascular and respiratory GP appointments following the launch of the CAZ.
 
· Carbon reduction of 150,000 tons reduction (CO2eq), across the lifetime of the CAZ
 
· Fleet transformation to cleanest taxi fleet in the UK with mainly petrol hybrid plus 800 electric vehicles, supported by Council grant scheme.
 
The CAZ has created a legally ringfenced revenue stream for Bradford MDC to develop a Sustainability Service, a team to deliver emission reduction projects, some of which will lever in private investment for clean growth in the City, examples of projects already underway are: 

Bradford Low Carbon Hydrogen Programme, the largest production and refuelling facility in the UK - a public/private partnership on Council land facilitated by the Councils chairing of the implementation board. 24MW of green Hydrogen. £0.5Bn from Government and £60m private investment (Home - Bradfordhydrogen)
 
Local Industrial Decarbonisation Project, decarbonising manufacturing. A Council led £1.1m IUK funded project resulting in Bradford Manufacturing Futures (Home | Bradford Cluster) Through collaborative innovation, as a not-for-profit organisation, Bradford Manufacturing Futures aims to champion manufacturers, facilitate the transition to net zero carbon by 2038 and support the sector's growth ambitions. A £700m programme of joint venture/capital investment to decarbonise the 1,200 manufacturing businesses employing 24,000 people and contributing £1.5billion to the local economy.
 
District Heat Network, 30 major buildings in the City Centre, a £75m project utilising £20m of Green heat network funding. The Council have provided £273k of funding to lever in additional private and public investment. City Hall will be the first Grade I listed building in the UK to join a heat network.
 
The Sustainability Service has also supported the development of a Clean Air Schools Programme with £500k grants for schools, e-bike scheme, a Climate Action Plan for the District, further health research, electric truck trials with local businesses and many other clean growth projects.
 
 The Sustainability Service collaborates with public and private partners to add value to the programme; reducing emissions, meeting the air quality objectives, improving health, providing green jobs, fuel security and prosperity for Bradford.

column17: The City of Fredericton uses its online engagement platform (Engage Fredericton/ Parlons-en Fredericton) to share knowledge and gather feedback from residents on a number of environmental projects and initiatives. We share information about projects or plan implementation through news releases, social media, and our website in addition to in person events, which are becoming more regular post-COVID. City staff regularly update a committee of City Council (the Environmental Stewardship Committee) in a public meeting. Presentations and recordings of the meetings are available via our website. We also host an Arc GIS based Environmental Dashboard that is regularly be updated. The Environmental Dashboard is a visual hub where residents can easily see our progress on climate issues that are important to them through graphs, maps, and links. March 2023, we received confirmation that 20.7m Home Upgrade Grant had been allocated to Cornwall, to improve 1,000 homes by March 2025. Alongside this allocation we also received confirmation of an allocation of 1.7m Social Housing Decarbonisation Fund for over 200 Cornwall Housing Limited homes, as well as other support for Coastline, Ocean and Live West homes totalling 3.7m, minimum of 420 homes. 

Home Upgrade Grant Phase 2 (HUG2) - treated 289 homes (2023 to March 2025). We were also invited to be a panellist at the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero representing grant recipients of HUG2. 

We completed 1268 homes with insulation and first-time central heating via Warm Homes Fund. 

Minimum Energy Efficiency Standard (MEES) - during 2024/25 95 properties were improved, there was a 307.3 carbon reduction, 2777 Standard Assessment Procedure (SAP) increase, 615 investigations and 175 private sector landlords were engaged with where properties were not MEES compliant. Cornwall Council, the Council of the Isles of Scilly and Isles of Scilly Integrated Care Board have signed a Civic University Agreement working in partnership with the Universities of Exeter and Falmouth. The agreement brings us together to work in collaboration and support Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly growth and prosperity. 

As part of the Together We Can: The Cornwall Plan 2020-50 there are four key commitments including Green Futures. 

Green Futures: Working for sustainable food, land and seas and a creative carbon zero economy, leaving more nature for future generations. Protecting and enhancing the environment is crucial for the future of our local communities and for our global climate and ecological survival. 

In Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly, with its rich and remarkable natural world all around us, the need to act for the environment is profoundly clear. The Universities have both committed to plans to achieve carbon neutrality and to support Cornwall and Isles of Scilly's transition to net zero. But more than that, both institutions understand that as places of advanced research and knowledge, and as educators of future global innovators, business leaders and entrepreneurs, we have an important role in driving policy and behaviour change and providing new ideas and solutions to difficult global problems. 

Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly have exceptional natural capital assets alongside unique strengths in minerals and mining expertise critical for the transition to net zero. Growth in our green and blue economy will support new jobs, while innovations in renewable and marine technology, exploitation of our critical mineral deposits will create new business opportunities. 

Additionally, the acceleration of the adoption of circular economy approaches, initiatives to promote behaviour change and new creative innovations to pivot Cornwall's dominant industry sectors to sustainability-led practices will put Cornwall at the forefront of the decarbonised national economy.

Cornwall Council is supporting projects and activities that will help Cornwall become carbon neutral and tackle climate change. We want to inspire and back projects that support the Council's climate emergency response and ambition to become carbon neutral by 2030. The following funding is available:

The Cornwall Climate & Nature Fund, is a partnership between Cornwall Council and Crowdfunder. It offers match funding support of up to £5,000 (and in exceptional cases, up to £15,000) for community-led crowdfunded projects across Cornwall that tackle climate change and/or promote nature recovery. 

To qualify, applicants must first raise at least 25 % of their crowdfunding target from 25+ individual backers - then Cornwall Council will match fund up to half the cost of the campaign target or up to a maximum of £5,000. Priority is given to initiatives with strong community impact and public access, addressing themes such as carbon reduction in homes and travel, renewable energy, habitat restoration, wildlife engagement, coastal conservation and tree planting. Successful projects must operate in Cornwall, follow council guidelines (e.g. tree planting projects require five years of care), and report outcomes clearly. The fund has backed 60 projects across Cornwall to date.

There are currently three open initiatives, facilitated by the Forest for Cornwall Team, that help communities to plant trees in their area:

Urban Tree Challenge Fund - for the improvement of green spaces and urban streets. Funded by the Forestry Commission and Forest for Cornwall. Over 500 trees have been planted so far across the County, with more planned for 2025/26.
 
Trees for Streets - we are working in partnership with this organisation and schemes will be funded by the Defra Shared Outcome Fund and Forest for Cornwall. We are starting with a pilot project in Camborne and will look to apply these learnings across other town councils with areas of low canopy cover and high population density. 
 
Forest for Cornwall funding - Our popular Back Garden Forest project will return this year, with thousands more free trees to be handed out. We also have other grants available, with up to £5,000 per eligible project to buy trees, protection, fencing, watering items etc. Back Garden Forest has distributed over 15,000 free trees to local communities and plans for 2025/26 are to host a further 10 giveaways across the county.

Nature Recovery & Regeneration and reintroductions: https://naturecios.org.uk/ The Council declared an ecological emergency on the 30th of November 2021 to drive action for nature recovery. The Cornwall & Isles of Scilly Local Nature Partnership is working to recover nature and put environment at the heart of decision-making. Having produced a pilot Local Nature Recovery Strategy in 2020-21, Cornwall has now developed a full statutory locally led Local Nature Recovery Strategy and it was adopted in March 2025. 
The strategy has been shaped by thousands of local views from environment professionals, farmers and growers, foresters, biological recorders, local businesses, Town and Parish Councils and others though a series of workshops, surveys, events and consultation.

The strategy provides guidance to support delivery of nature recovery across Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly so that we can have more nature which is bigger, better and joined up, which will help meet our local target of 30% of Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly's land, rivers and seas being well-managed for nature by 2030.

An important part of the strategy are the interactive maps. These maps have been developed to help understand where existing designations occur across Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly and, importantly, which areas can best take action to help restore nature. These consist of two zones: existing nature network and opportunity areas. The maps have been co-produced with the University of Exeter, working with the Environmental Records Centre for Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly (ERCCIS) and the Cornish Biodiversity Network and our biological recording community.

column17: Local Area Energy Planning (LAEP) - Awarded £500,000 from BEIS to deliver a Local Area Energy Plan to provide Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly with a practical roadmap as to how a net zero energy system can be achieved. Project commenced April 2023 and was completed in March 2025. The LAEP utilises a new, place-based approach that enables areas to develop their plans to decarbonise local energy systems. The Plan addresses the complex interactions of power, gas, heat, and transport, and the many ways in which future energy may be supplied, managed, and consumed within Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly. The Local Area Energy Plan is necessary to inform strategic planning, investments and decision-making, leading to the first net zero region that captures the 'benefits of decarbonising our local energy system to promote a prosperous and resilient economy and a just transition to a more sustainable future.' The plan for a resilient economy and a fair and inclusive society, will support the ambition for floating offshore wind and deep geothermal, inform future programmes to retrofit our homes and commercial and public buildings, investment in our energy and transport infrastructure, as well as identifying potential sites for renewables and energy storage to support sustainable growth and development for Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly. As a place-based plan for a low-carbon transition, the Plan will help facilitate the creation of an integrated position between planning and energy - enabling transport, housing and economic planning decisions relating to energy (supply and demand) to be viewed holistically and enable delivery against an agreed holistic strategy. Collaboration on the development of the plan has included working with key business stakeholders and also the establishment of a Residents' Energy Panel. Phase 1 (development of the LAEP) is now complete and Phase 2 (delivery) is underway.

The Climate Change and Health Tool has now been rolled out nationally as the Local Climate Adaptation Tool (LCAT). The LCAT is a national evidence-based resource to support local decision-makers, including public sector institutions to take climate adaptation action. The tool has been co-designed with over 50 local authority areas and provides data and evidence to help local areas understand the current and future climate, likely risks and impacts and adaptations needed. As well as highlighting impacts across sectors, it uses health as a lens to highlight the health impacts on communities. LCAT is a project between the University of Exeter and Cornwall Council, funded by Horizon Europe BlueAdapt project. 

LCAT is an online tool that supports decision-makers at a local level to take evidence-informed climate action. Designed with, and created for, local UK decision-makers. It provides information on: 
•	How local climates will change? 
•	What the likely hazards are (e.g flooding/ wildfires) 
•	What health and community impacts may occur as a result? 
•	Who will be most vulnerable and why? 
•	Which adaptations to consider? 

It has been created through: 
•	Co-design with stakeholders from across the UK, including multiple local authorities. 
•	Accessing data from open-source repositories to ensure LCAT remains free. 
•	Presenting data in accessible formats to ensure stakeholders can understand and use the information easily. 
•	Undertaking evidence reviews, beginning with the UK Climate Change Risk Assessment and the IPCC 2023 reports, followed by additional literature searches focusing on health and wellbeing impacts for LCAT. 
•	Identifying case studies to offer examples of action taken by local organisations. 
•	Developing the mDPSEEA framework and causal loop diagrams to show the evidence of climate change impacts on health and its complexity. 

As such, LCAT works to overcome many of the barriers stopping adaptation action by providing a free, easy to use tool which brings together trusted sources and evidence in one place. LCAT supports short, medium, and long-term thinking and multi-agency working and provides accompanying advice and guidance on what best practice looks like.

column17: Housing Decarbonisation Strategy: Following public consultation from July-September 2024 the Housing Decarbonisation Strategy was adopted in November 2024. The strategy looks at homes in Cornwall, to find the best ways to reduce harmful emissions, whilst keeping our homes warm in the winter, cool in the summer and making them affordable to run. As a council we want to make sure that everyone has access to the right advice and information. As a homeowner, tenant or landlord, having the best advice and support on the most effective ways to make green home improvements and ways to fund them is vital. Cornish homes are some of the oldest and leakiest in Europe! While they have a rich heritage, historically the array of building methods and materials used means they can be difficult to keep warm or cool, meaning they could be using more energy, making them more expensive to run. The Strategy aims to provide guidance on the benefits from living in a more energy efficient home: It's easier to keep it warm or cool when necessary. It needs less energy and so will be cheaper to run. It will be kinder to the planet using less energy lower emissions! It's a healthier place to live. Poor housing costs the NHS over 1 billion a year according to the Building Research Establishment (BRE). By making improvements that reduce carbon we can also help to ease the burden on the NHS and be kinder to the planet at the same time. The council works with housing providers to offer grants and initiatives, to eligible residents, to improve homes to make them more energy efficient and help them become cheaper to run. The strategy is looking at the best ways that we can support homeowners to make improvements and provide practical ways to support all of our residents. This could be with advice and information, useful online tools, signposting to alternative funding options to help people improve their own homes. Alongside these practical examples the Council is working with industries to attract and train people with the right skills and supporting the supply chain to help keep costs down.

Schools Net Zero Toolbox: https://letstalk.cornwall.gov.uk/schools-net-zero-tool-box. Working with schools across Cornwall, the Net Zero Toolkit has resources and tools to help schools and home education groups in their response to the climate and ecological emergency. Offering education and practical tips that can be used in schools and at home. A large number of Cornwall's schools are making a difference through the Schools Green Charter and their own climate action plans. We are working with schools across Cornwall to deliver the Eco Schools programme and Green Flag Award.

In 2025, Cornwall Council hosted a Schools Climate Conference, organised and delivered by the Education Business Partnership. The event brought together representatives from 140 schools and 22 nurseries, including school leaders, climate advisors, and partners such as Eco-Schools, Let's Go Zero, and Eco Rangers. Designed to support schools in developing Climate Action Plans, in line with the Department for Education's Sustainability and Climate Change Strategy (2023), which encourages all schools to appoint a Climate Lead and have a plan in place by the end of 2025, the event also featured contributions from organisations including Chefs in Schools, Cornwall Climate Care, RJ Working, Sustainable Food Cornwall, and the National Education Nature Park. The event led to a collation of carbon emission data from 49 schools, which allows us to have a better understanding of the actions that need to be taken. Feedback from the event will help shape future support for schools. Many attendees expressed interest in Cornwall Council's upcoming Green Schools programme, and several called for more strategic guidance, expert site visits, and opportunities to collaborate in smaller clusters.

In 2025 we supported the FIRST Lego League in Cornwall - a climate related innovation and STEM challenge. 60 schools in 2025 competed in the Cornwall FIRST Lego League. Supporting the development of STEM skills for our future generation in relation to climate related challenges. Each team has to undertake an innovation project to solve a problem - this year the theme was 'Ocean', including ocean health related to areas such as plastic pollution and marine life.

Urban Green Shoots has demonstrated how quickly Cornwall Council, in partnership with Cormac have responded to a funding opportunity to make widespread and long-lasting improvements for nature and people across across its environment estate. Since being awarded funding in late 2023, the project has implemented whole site schemes at 10 public open spaces and supported rewilding on urban verges across Camborne, Redruth and Liskeard. In January 2025 work commenced on the final site, at Barrowfields, Newquay, with the project completion date of March 2025. The Barrowfields scheme responds to the significance of the location as a site of scheduled prehistoric funerary monuments dating from the Late Neolithic period to the Late Bronze Age, known as bowl barrows. These features, which are a series of earth mounds are untouched by the planting and access improvements that will be delivered by Urban Green Shoots, and the project is also funding a new information board to help raise awareness about these ancient features that line the Newquay clifftops. The enhancements will improve access to and biodiversity/shelter at the viewpoint over Tolcarne beach, through improvements to the path and steps alongside a nature-rich Cornish hedge and wildflower meadow patches as well as installing lengths of colourful and scented plant beds along the walkway leading out to Bolowthas Corner. The scheme completed in March 2025. Our Let's Talk Cornwall pages promote a wide range of activities and opportunities for residents to be involved in projects across Cornwall from gardening groups, learning about bugs, hedgerow exploration, planting trees, primary schools, improving local parks and volunteering.

Creating a framework for blue natural capital investment in Cornwall. Blue Carbon Project: The Council is exploring the potential of blue carbon in Cornwall's coastal waters including seagrass, mud flats, salt marsh, maerl and kelp habitats. This project funded by the Natural Environment Investment Readiness Fund is helping to understand of blue carbon habitat extent and health and create a baseline of evidence to inform option in the future. 

Through collaborative work with our partners, the Project has resulted in;

Baselining: Undertaken surveys and analysis to understand the amount of carbon stored within kelp, maerl, saltmarsh and seagrass in two important Cornish coastal locations - Fal and Helford Estuary, and Mounts Bay.

Modelling: Modelled the potential for recovery of these blue carbon habitats, plus completed Natural Capital and ecosystem service risk assessments, at the two key sites.

Investing: Informed the development of options for increasing investment in the marine environment in Cornwall using the knowledge created through the results of the baseline and modelling research.

Cornwall Sustainability Awards (CSA) 

Cornwall Council uses the Cornwall Sustainability Awards (CSA) to engage with residents in several impactful ways:

Celebrating Local Efforts: The awards highlight the tireless work of community groups, charities, schools, businesses, social enterprises, and individuals in combating climate change and promoting sustainability. This recognition encourages more residents to participate in sustainable practices.

Public Involvement: Residents are invited to nominate projects or individuals for the awards, fostering a sense of community involvement and ownership. This inclusive approach ensures that a wide range of voices and efforts are acknowledged.

Educational Outreach: The CSA promotes awareness and education about sustainability through various categories that address different aspects of environmental stewardship, such as tree planting, circular economy, and environmental growth. This helps residents learn about and engage in sustainable practices.

Networking Opportunities: The awards ceremony and related events provide a platform for residents to connect with like-minded individuals and organisations, facilitating the exchange of ideas and collaboration on sustainability projects.

Incentivising Action: By recognising and rewarding sustainable initiatives, the CSA incentivises residents to adopt and innovate sustainable practices in their daily lives and businesses.

These strategies help Cornwall Council foster a culture of sustainability and community engagement across the region. 

Since CSA was launched in 2002 local Cornish businesses have been rewarded and recognised for their contribution towards sustainability, environmental growth, circular economy and carbon neutrality. Many have gone on to win national and international awards and become leaders in their field.

Cornwall Council's 'Carbon Neutral Cornwall Hive' is an online engagement platform for residents and businesses in Cornwall. The web platform provides a space for people to learn from each other and be inspired to reduce greenhouse gas emissions for better human and environmental health. It shows what the Council is doing and what other organisations and communities are leading on across Cornwall. There is a discussion forum, an ideas bank, blog posts, and sections that signpost people to useful information, resources, and funding opportunities to help get low carbon and environmental projects underway. In early 2025, a survey was sent out to gather views on the future development of the Hive and meetings with external organisations was held to hear how they use the Hive and what they think could be improved. The results of the survey and meetings are informing a refresh of the Hive platform to make it even more useful. .

Associated with the Carbon Neutral Cornwall Hive is the Council-led Carbon Neutral Cornwall Newsletter - https://www.cornwall.gov.uk/environment/climate-emergency/climate-emergency-news/ - that shares what is happening across Cornwall to reduce greenhouse gas emissions - for the benefit of residents and the environment. It goes out every two months and showcases what the Council is leading on as well as initiatives led by external organisations and partners. Regular correspondence and meetings with local organisations helps in deciding the content for the newsletter.

The Cornwall and Isles of Scilly Economic Forum (the Forum) is a group led by the private sector which advises Cornwall Council and the Council of the Isles of Scilly on economic priorities to create local jobs and drive growth. Members are drawn from a wide range of sectors and include representatives of Cornwall Council, which also provides the secretariat function. The Forum was created after the Government gave more control over economic development to local areas. Its goal is to provide a strong business perspective and local expertise to support the economic growth of Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly. The Forum helps shape local economic strategies, evaluates public sector initiatives, and attracts investment to support growth and development projects. It works with the Local Authorities on strategic economic planning for Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly and the associated implementation of action and investment plans to drive sustainable and responsible economic and inclusive growth. A sub group, the Cornwall and Isles of Scilly Workforce and Skills Board, is currently developing a Workforce and Skills Strategy for Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly.

column17: The UK Maerl Forum 2025, held on 25 April at the University of Exeter's Penryn Campus and online, was the first national event dedicated to the conservation of maerl beds—rare, slow-growing coralline red algae habitats vital for marine biodiversity and carbon storage. Co-hosted by Cornwall Council and Natural England, the forum brought together researchers, marine managers, conservationists, and policymakers from across the UK, Ireland, and Brittany to align efforts, share research, and develop a strategic action plan for maerl recovery in Cornwall and beyond. Key outcomes included the formation of a steering group, identification of priority actions, and commitment to ongoing monitoring and collaboration. The forum marked a significant step toward safeguarding one of the UK's most irreplaceable marine habitats through evidence-based conservation and inclusive partnerships.\nhttps://naturalengland.blog.gov.uk/2025/05/15/protecting-one-of-englands-rarest-marine-habitats-natural-englands-work-on-maerl/\n

In July 2021, Energy Saving Trust (EST) was commissioned by the North of Tyne Combined Authority (now North East Combined Authority) to develop a robust evidence base to inform the business case for a large scale housing retrofit programme. EST investigated two main retrofit scenarios. The Business as Usual (BAU) scenario assumed a continuation of historical trends in retrofit funding and delivery in the North of Tyne. The Net Zero scenario assumed extensive energy efficiency and lower carbon heating system upgrades with the goal of achieving net zero emissions. In order to achieve net zero, local retrofit rates across the NTCA will need to ramp up quickly. The Net Zero scenario will require over 80,000 homes to be retrofitted per year by 2027: more than 10 times the current rate. Additionally, the cost of achieving the Net Zero scenario will require an estimated 13bn in funding for the tri-borough area, beyond BAU funding sources (eg current and forthcoming grant funding). This has led to the creation of a one-stop-shop for retrofit across the three local authorities to achieve net-zero emissions across the housing stock. The EST report estimates that to achieve net-zero emissions in North Tyneside this will require the average home to attain a SAP score of 86 (EPC B), which will generate annual kWh savings of 1.4billion kWh across all homes and annual bill savings of 51million, taking the carbon footprint of the housing stock from 477,000tonnesCO2e to 44,100tCO2e - an emissions reduction of 91% against a 2021 emissions baseline. This entails retrofitting the average home with 7.2 energy efficiency measures and is estimated to cost 3.3billion for all homes in the borough. Most of this will need to be funded by homeowners, energy suppliers, and central government funding either directly to householders or channelled through schemes such as the Green Homes Grant/Sustainable Warmth and Social Housing Decarbonisation. Now firmly established, the One-Stop-Shop is the critical enabler to retrofit at scale across all homes, regardless of income, providing end-to-end project management and signposting to appropriately qualified installers, recognised technologies, energy modelling and financing options. Funding will need to be sought to continue the one stop shop beyond the pilot end date of March 2025

column17: The WMCA has a circular economy delivery programme which is guided by a circular economy routemap published in 2021. The circular economy routemap aims to encourage materials efficiency in the West Midlands economy through an initial focus on three strategically important areas: manufacturing, construction, and food. The circular economy programme has two main areas which has seen extensive industry collaboration to date, the industrial symbiosis project and subsequent West Midlands Resource Reuse Network, and the delivery of Zero Waste Construction Hubs. Firstly, the West Midlands Resource Reuse Network is a materials focused business support programme currently being piloted directly with businesses in the region. The aim of the Network is to support businesses to become more materials efficient by creating a network of businesses engaging in the mutually beneficial transfer of waste and resources, such that one company's waste becomes another's raw material. Setting up and delivering the Network has required substantial levels of collaboration with the business community in the region. The delivery of the Network is based on a business case that the WMCA completed in 2022, which aimed to co-create the project with the regional business community and industry groups. The second area of circular economy delivery that has required extensive business collaboration is the delivery of the Zero Waste Construction Hubs project. The Zero Waste Construction Hubs project aims to reduce the amount of waste produced by the construction sector by developing the infrastructure required to facilitate materials recovery from active construction sites. The WMCA conducted a feasibility study which engaged heavily with the region's construction sector to assess the feasibility of the concept in the region. Following the confirmation of feasibility, the WMCA convened a community interest company and a local charity to deliver the first pilot hub in Wolverhampton, which successfully opened in July 2024.\n\nIn 2026, the WMCA will feature as a headline partner in the delivery of Circular Economy UK 2026, a first of its kind conference that will bring together local, regional, and national, stakeholders from the public and private sectors to identify how collaboration can further support and accelerate the uptake of the circular economy.

In 2012, a MOA was forged among the City Government of Ligao, Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources, 3rd District of Albay House of Representative, Philippine Army, Philippine National Police, Department of Environment and Natural Resources for the creation of Ligao City Illegal Fishing and Fisheries and Aquatic Resources Protection Task Force.
The Chairman is the Ligao City Mayor; Vice-Chairman - BFAR 5; and the members of the task force are the 3rd District Congressman, Philippine Army, DENR, City PNP Chief of Police, Punong Barangays of Maonon, Cabarian and Catburawan, Deputy Fish Warden Team Leader and City Fisheries and Aquatic Resources Management Council (CFARMC). 
The City of Ligao provides subsistence and MOOE to the members of the Bantay-Dagat-CAFGU contingent; provide enforcers with the necessary equipment, supplies and craft for seabore patrolling; coordinate with National Government Agencies on the implementation of the Fisheries Code and submit reports to the MOA parties on status of task force.
BFAR 5 assist in the apprehension and prosecution of violators together with competent enforcement agencies; assist in law enforcement and train personnel on identification of illegally-caugh fish; safeguard confiscated items; regular updating of information and new provisions of fishery laws; in coordination with DENR, assist the City of Ligao in marine and aquatic resources preservation and environmental aspects; provide technical assistance in the promotion of fisheries and aquatic development; provide seaborne patrolling water craft for patrol use by Bantay-Dagat-CAFGU contingent; submit updates and reports to the City Mayor, Congressman and MOA parties; and deputize CAFGU contigents as Fish Warden.
The 3rd District of Albay Representative provides financial support to LGU for the operation and management of the Bantay-Dagat-CAFGU contingent; makes representation with National Agencies to support fully the implementation of the Fisheries Code; Provide the Barangay units with financial support to upgrade the barangay capabilities for the promotion for the management, promotion, and management of fisheries and aquatic resources and provide assistance in the capacity building of barangay enforcement of fishery laws; conduct inquiries, public hearings and investigations in aid to legislation on the matter of the Fisheries Code of 1998 and introduce legislation in pursuit of the welfare of fisherfolks and coastal residents.
Philippine Army (PA) provide supervision and proper conduct by Bantay-Dagat-CAFGU contingent; provide the contingent with guidelines on the Rule of Engagement with firearms; provide for subsistence allowance in the amount of Php90.00 per day or the same subsistence allowance per day of regular AFP troops as provided by law; assist in the conduct of apprehensions and seaborne patrolling; and provide security protection to Bantay-Dagat-CAFGU contingent.
Philippine National Police provides assistance in the enforcement and apprehension of violators of teh Fisheries Code; provide assistance in the preparation, filing of complaint and in the prosecution of case; serve warrant of arrest; and submit reports to the Mayor and MOA parties.
Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) V assists the City of Ligao in the implemention of programs relative to the protection, conservation, management, utilization and regulation of environment and natural resources; provide technical assistance and capacity building in the promotion of forest (e.g. mangrove, etc.)and wildlife resources development and pollution control (air, water and other resources); update regularly of policy issuances; and assist in the enforcement of environmental laws and deputize competent individuals who shall undergo the prescribed training for SDENRO or Wildlife Enforcement Officer.
